definition_zh: 自动的；无意识的，习惯性的；必然的
definition_en: working by itself without a person, done without thinking, or certain to happen as a result
core_image: 门在人走近时自己滑开，没有谁去推
scene: 手里拎着东西走到门口，门先一步让开。The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
sceneCN: 这里 automatic 是「自动的」（第 1 个义项：机器自己运作）；句意是这些门是自动的，不用手碰。

pos.zh: 形容词：自动的；无意识的；必然的

derivatives.zh: 副词：自动地；不假思索地

senses.title: Machine works alone
senses.definition: working by itself without a person operating it
senses.definitionCN: 不需要人操作就能自己运转的
senses.example: The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
senses.exampleCN: 这些门是自动的，不用手碰。
senses.why: Greek automatos described something acting of its own will, and machines took over that sense: the mechanism plays the role of the will.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 automatos 描述「按自己的意愿行动」，机器接过了这层意思：机械装置扮演了意愿的角色。

senses.title: Done without thinking
senses.definition: done as a habit or reflex, without conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 作为习惯或本能做出，不经思考的
senses.example: Answering the phone is automatic for her.
senses.exampleCN: 接电话对她来说是不假思索的事。
senses.why: A person can also run on autopilot: the body acts by itself, so the machine word is applied to human habit.
senses.whyCN: 人也能靠「自动驾驶」运转：身体自己动起来，于是这个机器词被用到人的习惯上。

senses.title: Certain to follow
senses.definition: certain to happen as a natural result of something
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事的自然结果必然发生的
senses.example: A price cut means an automatic rise in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 降价必然带来销量上升。
senses.why: If a result follows a cause with no choice involved, it is automatic in the logical sense, like a machine that cannot do otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果毫无选择地跟着原因出现，它在逻辑意义上就是自动的，像一台不可能有别的动作的机器。

intro.en: Automatic first described things that move by their own will.
intro.cn: automatic 最初描述「按自己的意愿行动」的东西。

items.en: autos meant 'self'.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」。

items.en: automatos meant 'acting of itself'.
items.cn: automatos 意为「自行动作的」。

items.en: automaton named a self-moving device.
items.cn: automaton 指能自己活动的装置。

items.en: French automatique applied the idea to machinery.
items.cn: 法语 automatique 把这个概念用到机械上。

items.en: English extended it to habits and inevitable results.
items.cn: 英语又把它扩展到习惯动作与必然结果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auto- prefix; the near-meaning group gives words for machine-like action.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auto- 前缀；近义组是表示机械式动作的词。

entries.definition: done by a machine or like a machine

normalIntro.en: Automatic moves the idea of self from a person to a machine, then back to a habit.
normalIntro.cn: automatic 把「自己」这个念头从人移到机器，再移回人的习惯。

normal.en: The prefix auto- means self, so automatic means acting by itself.
normal.cn: 前缀 auto- 意为「自己」，所以 automatic 就是自己动作。

normal.en: Automatic doors and automatic updates are the most common modern uses.
normal.cn: 自动门与自动更新是它最常见的现代用法。

normal.en: An automatic response is a reflex, not a decision.
normal.cn: automatic response 是本能反应，不是决定。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ally: automatically.
normal.cn: 副词形式加 -ally，变成 automatically。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with automated, which describes a process converted to machines.
normal.cn: 不要与 automated 混淆，后者描述被改成机器运作的流程。

abstract.en: See glass doors part before a hand can reach them.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃门在手伸到之前就分开。

abstract.en: See a hand pick up a ringing phone with no thought.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手想都没想就接起响着的电话。

abstract.en: See one falling domino knock the next without choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一块倒下的骨牌毫无选择地撞倒下一块。

examples.en: The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
examples.cn: 这些门是自动的，不用手碰。

examples.en: Answering the phone is automatic for her.
examples.cn: 接电话对她来说是不假思索的事。

examples.en: A price cut means an automatic rise in sales.
examples.cn: 降价必然带来销量上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: auto（自己）加 -matic：机器自己动是自动，人不动脑就做是习惯，结果不由人挑就是必然。

root: 源自希腊语 automatos「自行动作的」，经 automaton「自动装置」与法语 automatique 进入英语；由机器自己运转，引申为人不假思索的习惯动作，再引申为必然出现的结果。

sensesIntro.en: A machine, a habit and a consequence can all be automatic.
sensesIntro.cn: 机器、习惯和后果，都可以是 automatic。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that opens before a hand touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：手还没碰到，门已经开了。

intro.en: The prefix auto-, 'self', builds automatic, automate and automation.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto- 意为「自己」，构成 automatic、automate 与 automation。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, so automatic belongs with Greek-made words like autonomy.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根来自希腊语，所以 automatic 与 autonomy 这类希腊来源的词同属一族。

items.meaning: a self-moving machine or a lifeless actor
items.meaningCN: 自动装置；机械行事的人

items.meaning: a car or a self-working setting

definition_zh: 自动地；不假思索地；必然地
definition_en: in a way that works by itself, without thinking, or as a necessary result
core_image: 文件刚改完，云端自己打了一个勾
scene: 编辑文档时手一顿，标题栏已经显示保存完成。The file saves automatically every minute.
sceneCN: 这里 automatically 是「自动地」（第 1 个义项：机器自己完成）；句意是文件每分钟自动保存。

pos.zh: 副词：自动地；不假思索地；必然地

senses.title: By machine, unaided
senses.definition: by a machine or system working without a person's action
senses.definitionCN: 由机器或系统在人不出手的情况下完成
senses.example: The file saves automatically every minute.
senses.exampleCN: 文件每分钟自动保存。
senses.why: The adverb describes the manner of the action: no hand is involved, because the mechanism supplies the movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述动作的方式：没有手参与，因为动作由机械装置提供。

senses.title: Without thinking
senses.definition: as an unthinking habit or reflex
senses.definitionCN: 作为不经思考的习惯或本能
senses.example: She automatically assumes the worst.
senses.exampleCN: 她总是想当然地往最坏处想。
senses.why: The machine image moves to the mind: a habit runs on its own, so the person reaches the conclusion with no deliberate step.
senses.whyCN: 机器的意象转到心里：习惯自行运转，于是人没有经过刻意的步骤就得出这个结论。

senses.title: As a sure result
senses.definition: as a result that must follow
senses.definitionCN: 作为必定随之出现的结果
senses.example: Prices automatically rise when supply falls.
senses.exampleCN: 供给下降时，价格必然上涨。
senses.why: When one change forces another with no alternative, the adverb marks that inevitability rather than any machine.
senses.whyCN: 当一个变化迫使另一个变化、别无选择时，这个副词标记的是那种必然性，而不是任何机器。

intro.en: Automatically is simply automatic with the adverb ending added.
intro.cn: automatically 就是 automatic 加上副词词尾。

items.en: automatos meant 'acting of itself'.
items.cn: automatos 意为「自行动作的」。

items.en: French automatique described self-moving machinery.
items.cn: 法语 automatique 描述自行运转的机械。

items.en: English automatic carried the sense of working alone.
items.cn: 英语 automatic 带有「自行运作」的意思。

items.en: The ending -ally turned the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.cn: 词尾 -ally 把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Software made the word a daily sight on screens.
items.cn: 软件让这个词成了屏幕上每天都能见到的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the automatic family; the near-meaning group gives other manner adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组属于 automatic 词族；近义组是其他方式副词。

normalIntro.en: Automatically answers how: by itself, without thought, or by necessity.
normalIntro.cn: automatically 回答「怎样」：自己来、不经思考，或必然如此。

normal.en: Take automatic and add -ally, keeping the final c.
normal.cn: 把 automatic 加上 -ally，保留词尾的 c。

normal.en: Software contexts make automatically the most common form you will read.
normal.cn: 在软件语境里，automatically 是你最常读到的形式。

normal.en: Automatically assume is a polite way to describe a wrong unthinking judgment.
normal.cn: automatically assume 是描述「想当然」这种错误判断的委婉说法。

normal.en: The adjective drops the -ally: an automatic reply.
normal.cn: 形容词形式去掉 -ally：automatic reply。

normal.en: Do not say automaticly; the correct ending is -ally.
normal.cn: 不要写成 automaticly，正确词尾是 -ally。

abstract.en: See a cloud icon put a tick on a page by itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一个云端图标自己在页面上打了个勾。

abstract.en: See a hand reach for a ringing phone before the eyes look up.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛还没抬起来，手已经伸向响着的电话。

abstract.en: See one scale tip as soon as a weight is added.
abstract.cn: 想象砝码一加上去，天平立刻倾斜。

examples.en: The file saves automatically every minute.
examples.cn: 文件每分钟自动保存。

examples.en: She automatically assumes the worst.
examples.cn: 她总是想当然地往最坏处想。

examples.en: Prices automatically rise when supply falls.
examples.cn: 供给下降时，价格必然上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: automatic 加 -ally：机器不用人管是自动地，人不用脑是习惯地，结果不用挑是必然地。

root: 由 automatic 加副词词尾 -ally 构成；automatic 源自希腊语 automatos「自行动作的」，经法语 automatique 进入英语；现代软件语境让这个词成为日常高频副词。

sensesIntro.en: The same adverb can describe a machine, a habit and an unavoidable result.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词既能描述机器，也能描述习惯，还能描述无法避免的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page that ticks itself saved.
core.cn: 核心意象：页面自己打上「已保存」的勾。

intro.en: The prefix auto-, 'self', plus -ally makes automatically a manner adverb.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto-「自己」加上 -ally，使 automatically 成为方式副词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, shared with automatic and autonomy.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根来自希腊语，与 automatic、autonomy 共用。

definition_zh: 汽车，机动车；（作定语）汽车的
definition_en: a road vehicle with an engine, especially a car, or used before a noun to mean relating to cars
core_image: 一辆四轮车自己发动，载着人离开门口
scene: 老照片里，街上的马车旁边第一次停了一辆不用马拉的车。The automobile changed how cities grew.
sceneCN: 这里 automobile 是「汽车」（第 1 个义项：四轮机动车）；句意是汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：汽车的；机动车的

senses.title: Engine-powered road car
senses.definition: a road vehicle with its own engine, especially a passenger car
senses.definitionCN: 自带发动机的道路车辆，尤指载客汽车
senses.example: The automobile changed how cities grew.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。
senses.why: The word was coined when engineers needed a formal name for a carriage that moves itself, so it names the machine rather than the everyday car.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要为「自己能走的马车」取一个正式名字，于是造出这个词，所以它指的是机器本身，而不是日常口语里的车。

senses.title: Car as a modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean of or relating to cars
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示与汽车有关的
senses.example: He works in the automobile industry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在汽车行业工作。
senses.why: In compounds the noun loses its plural and works like an adjective, naming a whole field such as industry, age or accident.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词里这个名词不用复数，起形容词作用，用来命名整个领域，如工业、时代或事故。

intro.en: Automobile is a French-made word meaning self-moving.
intro.cn: automobile 是法语造的，意思是「自己能动的」。

items.en: autos meant 'self'.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」。

items.en: mobile came from Latin mobilis, 'able to move'.
items.cn: mobile 来自拉丁语 mobilis，意为「能移动的」。

items.en: automobile was coined for a self-moving vehicle.
items.cn: automobile 被造出来指自行移动的车辆。

items.en: English adopted it as the formal word for a motor car.
items.cn: 英语在 1897 年采用它作为汽车的正式说法。

items.en: Everyday speech shortened it to auto and car.
items.cn: 日常口语把它缩短成 auto 与 car。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auto- prefix; the near-meaning group gives words for road vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auto- 前缀；近义组是表示道路车辆的词。

entries.definition: a road vehicle for a few passengers
a car, in older British use

normalIntro.en: Automobile is a description turned into a name: self plus moving.
normalIntro.cn: automobile 是把一个描述变成了名字：自己加移动。

normal.en: Break it into auto, self, and mobile, moving.
normal.cn: 拆成 auto「自己」和 mobile「可移动的」。

normal.en: It is the formal word; car is the everyday one.
normal.cn: 它是正式说法，car 是日常说法。

normal.en: Before another noun it keeps the singular: automobile industry.
normal.cn: 放在另一名词前时用单数：automobile industry。

normal.en: The short form auto belongs to American English.
normal.cn: 缩略形式 auto 属于美式英语。

normal.en: Automotive is the adjective used for the whole industry.
normal.cn: automotive 是用于整个行业的形容词。

abstract.en: See a carriage roll forward with no horse in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆马车向前走，前面却没有马。

abstract.en: See a factory line of identical bodies in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂流水线上一排一模一样的车身。

abstract.en: See an old photo of a street half horse, half engine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张老照片，街上半是马车，半是汽车。

examples.en: The automobile changed how cities grew.
examples.cn: 汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。

examples.en: He works in the automobile industry.
examples.cn: 他在汽车行业工作。

examples.en: The museum keeps an early automobile in working order.
examples.cn: 博物馆保存着一辆仍能开动的早期汽车。

dict_mnemonic.text: auto（自己）加 mobile（能动的）：不用马拉、自己会走的车，就是 automobile；放到名词前就表示「汽车的」。

root: 由希腊语 autos「自己」与拉丁语 mobilis「能移动的」组合，经法语 automobile 进入英语；十九世纪末用来命名不用马拉的机动车，后来日常口语简化为 auto 与 car。

sensesIntro.en: The name describes the machine, and the same word can label the whole industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名字描述机器本身，同一个词也能标注整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carriage that moves with no horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆不用马拉却自己在走的马车。

intro.en: The prefix auto-, 'self', joins mobile, 'moving', to make automobile.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto-「自己」加 mobile「可移动的」，构成 automobile。

latinIntro.en: The moving half is Latin mobilis; the self half is Greek autos.
latinIntro.cn: 「移动」那一半来自拉丁语 mobilis，「自己」那一半来自希腊语 autos。

definition_zh: 自治；自主；自主权；自主性
definition_en: the power or right to govern oneself or to act independently
core_image: 手术室里主刀医生按判断改动切口，没有等行政人员签字
scene: 手术室里，主刀医生按自己的判断改动了切口位置，没有等行政人员批准。The hospital defends the autonomy of its surgical teams.
sceneCN: 这里指专业人员在自己的领域内自主决定（第 4 个义项：专业自主权）；句意为医院维护外科团队的自主权。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、器械台、病历夹、签字笔。

pos.zh: 名词：自治；自主；自主权（不可数，指具体自治体时偶作可数）

derivatives.zh: 由希腊词根加形容词词尾构成，义为「自治的；自主的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「自主地」
由词根加表示人的词尾构成，义为「自治主张者」
由表示「他者」的前缀加同一词根构成，义为「他律」

senses.title: Self-government of a region
senses.definition: the right of a region or people to govern its own affairs within a larger state
senses.definitionCN: 地区或民族在大国之内管理自身事务的权利
senses.example: The province gained autonomy over its schools and hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 该省获得了管理本省学校与医院的自治权。
senses.why: The Greek word joins self and law, so autonomy is literally the power to give oneself law.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词由「自我」与「法律」合成，因此自治字面上就是给自己立法的权力。

senses.title: Personal autonomy
senses.definition: the capacity of a person to make decisions without being controlled by others
senses.definitionCN: 个人不受他人控制而自行决定的能力
senses.example: Patients value autonomy in decisions about their own care.
senses.exampleCN: 病人珍视在自身照护上的自主决定权。
senses.why: Political self-rule became a model for the individual ruling himself.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的自治成了个人自我治理的模型。

senses.title: Institutional autonomy
senses.definition: the freedom of an institution such as a university to set its own rules
senses.definitionCN: 大学等机构自行制定规则的自由
senses.example: The reform protected the autonomy of universities in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革保护了大学在招聘上的自治。
senses.why: An institution with its own law is one that can choose its members and methods.
senses.whyCN: 拥有自身规则的机构，才能选择自己的成员与方法。

senses.title: Professional autonomy
senses.definition: the freedom of trained professionals to make expert judgments without outside direction
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练的专业人员在不受外部指挥下作出专业判断的自由
senses.example: The college defended the autonomy of surgeons in the operating room.
senses.exampleCN: 该院维护外科医生在手术室里的自主权。
senses.why: Expertise is useless if the judgment can be overridden by administrators.
senses.whyCN: 如果专业判断能被行政人员推翻，专业知识就失去作用。

senses.title: Learner autonomy
senses.definition: the capacity of a student to plan and monitor his or her own learning
senses.definitionCN: 学生自行规划与监控学习的能力
senses.example: The course builds autonomy by letting students choose their reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课通过让学生自选读物来培养自主性。
senses.why: Education borrowed the political word for the student who sets his own targets.
senses.whyCN: 教育学借来这个政治词，指为自己设定目标的学生。

senses.title: Job autonomy
senses.definition: the degree of freedom an employee has in deciding how to do the work
senses.definitionCN: 雇员在决定如何完成工作上拥有的自由程度
senses.example: Higher autonomy at work predicted lower staff turnover.
senses.exampleCN: 工作中的自主权越高，员工流失率越低。
senses.why: Management research measures autonomy as control over method and schedule.
senses.whyCN: 管理学把自主权测量为对方法与进度的控制。

senses.title: Machine autonomy
senses.definition: the ability of a system to operate and decide without a human operator
senses.definitionCN: 系统无需人操作即可运行与决策的能力
senses.example: Engineers tested the autonomy of the vehicle in heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在暴雨中测试了这辆车的自主能力。
senses.why: Self-rule was extended to machines that set their own course of action.
senses.whyCN: 「自治」被扩展到能自行决定行动路线的机器。

senses.title: Moral autonomy
senses.definition: the capacity to act according to a law one gives oneself, rather than external pressure
senses.definitionCN: 按自己给自己立的法则而非外部压力行动的能力
senses.example: Moral autonomy requires judging for oneself rather than obeying blindly.
senses.exampleCN: 道德自主要求自己判断，而不是盲目服从。
senses.why: Moral philosophy turned the image of self-legislation into a standard of dignity.
senses.whyCN: 道德哲学把「自我立法」的形象变成尊严的标准。

senses.title: Patient autonomy in medical ethics
senses.titleCN: 医疗伦理中的病人自主
senses.definition: the principle that a patient's informed choice governs treatment
senses.definitionCN: 病人的知情选择主导治疗方案的原则
senses.example: Consent forms put patient autonomy before clinical convenience.
senses.exampleCN: 知情同意书把病人自主放在临床便利之前。
senses.why: Medical ethics needed a principle that could overrule a clinician's recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 医疗伦理需要一个能推翻临床建议的原则。

intro.en: Autonomy came into English from Greek autonomia, the state of having one's own law, built from autos, self, and nomos, law or custom. It reached English through French in the seventeenth century, first as a word about states and later about persons.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 autonomia「拥有自己的法律的状态」，由表示「自我」的词与表示「法律、习俗」的词构成。它在十七世纪进入英语，最先用于国家，后来才用于个人。

items.en: The pronoun meant self, and it supplies the first element in autonomy, automatic and autograph.
items.cn: 这个词意为「自我」，是「自治」「自动」「亲笔」等词的第一个成分。

items.en: The noun meant law, custom or rule, and it also stands behind economy and astronomy.
items.cn: 这个名词意为法律、习俗、规则，也是「经济」与「天文」等词的成分。

items.en: The noun described a community that lived under its own laws rather than those of a ruler.
items.cn: 这个名词描述按自己的法律而非统治者法律生活的共同体。

items.en: French carried the political word into wider European use in the early modern period.
items.cn: 法语在近代早期把这个政治词带进更广的欧洲使用。

items.en: English first applied it to states and churches, and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语最初把它用于国家与教会，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later centuries applied it to individuals, professions, learners, patients and machines.
items.cn: 后来的几个世纪把它扩展到个人、专业、学习者、病人与机器。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek elements; the second group names neighbouring kinds of independence.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语成分；第二组是相邻的独立概念。

entries.definition: The adjective for self-governing or self-directing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为自治的、自主的。

entries.definition: A supporter of autonomy for a region or group.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张地区或群体自治的人。

entries.definition: Self-acting, from the same first element but a different second one.
entries.definitionCN: 指自动的；共享第一个成分，但第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: Rule by another, the opposite of self-rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指由他者支配，与自治相反。

entries.definition: Freedom from control by another, often political.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受他人控制，多用于政治。

entries.definition: The act of governing oneself, used mostly of territories.
entries.definitionCN: 指自我治理，多用于地区。

entries.definition: Supreme authority over a territory, stronger than autonomy.
entries.definitionCN: 指对领土的最高权力，比自治更强。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being constrained.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束的一般状态。

entries.definition: The right of a people to choose its own status.
entries.definitionCN: 指民族自行决定自身地位的权利。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two Greek parts, self and law, and the domains that borrowed them.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个希腊成分「自我」与「法律」，以及借用它们的各个领域。

normal.en: Autonomy is self plus law: the power to give yourself the rule you live by.
normal.cn: 自治就是「自我」加「法律」：给自己立下所循规则的权力。

normal.en: A province with autonomy writes its own school rules, which is the political sense.
normal.cn: 拥有自治的省份自己写学校规则，这是政治义。

normal.en: A surgeon with autonomy decides the incision without waiting for an administrator.
normal.cn: 有自主权的外科医生自行决定切口，不必等行政人员。

normal.en: A learner with autonomy chooses the reading list, and a worker with autonomy chooses the method.
normal.cn: 自主的学习者自选书单，自主的工人自选方法。

normal.en: A vehicle with autonomy chooses its own route, extending self-rule to machines.
normal.cn: 自主的车辆自选路线，把自治扩展到机器。

abstract.en: Every autonomy is a border drawn twice: once around the self, once around the law.
abstract.cn: 每一种自主都是画了两次的边界：一次围住自我，一次围住法律。

abstract.en: To be autonomous is to be the author of the rule one obeys, and also its prisoner.
abstract.cn: 自主意味着既是所循规则的作者，也是它的囚徒。

abstract.en: Institutions ask for autonomy in the same words that peoples once used for independence.
abstract.cn: 机构索要自主时用的词，与民族当年索要独立时用的是同一套。

examples.en: The treaty granted autonomy to the coastal region.
examples.cn: 条约给予沿海地区自治权。

examples.en: Clinical staff resisted limits on their autonomy in treatment decisions.
examples.cn: 临床人员抵制对治疗决策自主权的限制。

examples.en: The software was designed to operate with greater autonomy in remote areas.
examples.cn: 这款软件被设计成能在偏远地区以更高自主性运行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥托诺米」——自己给自己定规矩，不用别人管，就是「自治、自主」：自治、自主权

root: 经法语来自希腊语 autonomia「拥有自己的法律的状态」，由 autos「自我」与 nomos「法律、习俗」构成；十七世纪进入英语，最初用于国家与教会，后扩展到个人、专业、学习者、病人与机器，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses apply self-rule to a region, a person, an institution, a profession, a learner, a job, a machine, a moral agent and a patient.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把「自我立法」用在地区、个人、机构、专业、学习者、工作、机器、道德主体与病人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an operating lamp above a table, and a surgeon changing the incision line without waiting for a signature.
core.cn: 核心意象：手术台上方的灯，以及不等签字就改动切口的医生。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL SELF-RULE: a region lives under laws it makes.
branches.cn: 政治自治：地区按自己制定的法律生活。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL AND MORAL SELF-RULE: a person decides, judges and consents.
branches.cn: 个人与道德的自治：个人自行决定、判断与同意。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE LEARNER: a body or a student sets its own course.
branches.cn: 机构与学习者：机构或学生自定方向。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONAL AND THE WORKER: expert judgment and control over method.
branches.cn: 专业与工作者：专业判断，以及对方法的控制。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a system that selects its own course of action.
branches.cn: 机器：自行选择行动路线的系统。

intro.en: The word is Greek in both halves, self and law, with only a noun ending added in English.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都出自希腊语：自我与法律，英语只加了一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin root for this word; the Latin forms listed are later borrowings from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有本土拉丁词根；列出的拉丁形式是后来从希腊语借入的。

items.example: It is the first element of autonomy and automatic.
items.exampleCN: 它是「自治」与「自动」的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of autonomy.
items.exampleCN: 它是「自治」的第二个成分。

items.meaning: the state of having one's own law
items.meaningCN: 拥有自己的法律的状态
items.exampleCN: 这个名词描述自治的共同体。

items.example: French carried the word into wider European use.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带进更广的欧洲使用。

items.example: English uses it for states, people and machines.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它指国家、人与机器。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin adjective ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加了拉丁形容词词尾。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the Greek noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由希腊名词词干构成形容词。

items.example: It forms the adverb of manner.
It appears in automatic and autobiography.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在「自动」与「自传」等词里。

items.example: It forms the word for an advocate of autonomy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指自治主张者的名词。

加副词词尾构成，义为「自主地」

definition_zh: v. 有益于；起作用；（用于反身句式）利用；n. 效用；益处（多见于固定短语）
definition_en: To be of use or help; reflexively, to make use of an offer or chance; as a noun, use or benefit, now mainly in set phrases.
core_image: 手里那点力气到底顶不顶用
scene: 律师劝他利用这次免费复核的机会。The lawyer urged him to avail himself of the free review.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：avail oneself of 表示利用某个机会或条件，是这个词最常见的现代用法。

senses.title: To be of use
senses.definition: to help or produce a useful effect, often used in the negative
senses.definitionCN: 有所帮助或产生有用的效果，常用于否定句
senses.example: Protests availed nothing against the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议对该决定毫无作用。
senses.why: Avail joins a-, to, with val, worth, so it literally means to be worth something to someone.
senses.whyCN: avail 由 a-「向」与 val「价值」构成，字面就是「对某人有价值」。

senses.title: To make use of
senses.definition: in the reflexive pattern avail oneself of, to take advantage of an offer, chance or facility
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身句式，指利用某个机会、条件或设施
senses.example: Few residents availed themselves of the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有居民利用这项补助。
senses.why: If something is worth something to you, you can turn that worth to account, which is exactly what the reflexive pattern says.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物对你有价值，你就可以把这份价值用起来，这正是反身句式所表达的意思。

senses.title: Use or benefit
senses.definition: as a noun, help or advantage, surviving chiefly in set phrases of little use
senses.definitionCN: 作名词指帮助或好处，主要保留在表示收效甚微的固定短语中
senses.example: All their pleading was of no avail.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有的恳求都毫无用处。
senses.why: The noun kept the old sense of worth, and because it froze inside set phrases it now sounds formal.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「价值」这一旧义，又因固定在短语内部，如今听起来偏正式。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail, from Old French valoir, to be worth, from Latin valere, to be strong or worth; the same root gives value and valid.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail，出自古法语 valoir「有价值」，源自拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」；同一词根产生 value 与 valid。

items.en: A root meaning to be strong lies behind words of worth, health and power.
items.cn: 一个表示「强健」的词根支撑着价值、健康与力量类的词。

items.en: Latin valere meant to be strong, to be well, and hence to be worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为「强健、安好」，进而指「有价值」。

items.en: Old French valoir kept the sense of being worth a price or a benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 保留了「值某个价钱或有某种好处」的意思。

items.en: With a-, to, added, avaloir meant to be of profit to someone.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avaloir，意为「对某人有益」。

items.en: Middle English availen meant to help or profit, both as verb and noun.
items.cn: 中古英语 availen 意为「有益、有帮助」，动词名词皆可。

items.en: The bare verb faded, leaving the reflexive pattern and phrases meaning in vain.
items.cn: 单独的动词用法衰退，留下反身句式与表示徒劳的短语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the val family and two words of similar sound; the near-meaning group lists plainer words for being of use.
note.cn: 形近组保留 val 词族和两个读音相近的词；近义组列出表示「有用」的更平易的词。

entries.definition: Ready to be used or got.
To prove stronger, to win through.
To make things easier for someone.
To do good to, or the good done.

normalIntro.en: Avail is a- plus vail, a cousin of value: to be worth something to you, or to turn that worth to use.
normalIntro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail，与 value 同族：对你有价值，或把这份价值用起来。

normal.en: The live pattern is avail oneself of.
normal.cn: 仍在使用的句式是反身加 of 的结构。

normal.en: To no avail means the effort failed.
normal.cn: 表示徒劳的短语说明努力白费。

normal.en: Of little avail means almost useless.
normal.cn: 表示收效甚微的短语意为几乎无用。

normal.en: The root val also gives value and valid.
normal.cn: 词根 val 也产生 value 与 valid。

normal.en: Avail is formal; use is everyday.
normal.cn: avail 偏正式，use 是日常用词。

abstract.en: Picture strength that finally moves a weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一股终于推动重物的力气。

abstract.en: Imagine an open door you decide to walk through.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇敞开的门，你决定走进去。

abstract.en: Think of shouting into wind that ignores you.
abstract.cn: 想象对着不理你的风喊话。

examples.en: She availed herself of the shuttle bus.
examples.cn: 她利用了那趟班车。

examples.en: Their warnings availed little.
examples.cn: 他们的警告收效甚微。

examples.en: He argued for an hour, to no avail.
examples.cn: 他争了一小时，徒劳无功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ vail（与 value 同族，「价值」）——对你有价值就是 avail「有用」，把这份价值用起来就是「利用」。

root: 拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」经古法语 valoir 加 a-「向」成 avaloir「对……有益」，入中古英语作 availen；现代主要保留反身句式与表示徒劳的固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses turn on worth: something being worth something to you, your turning that worth to use, and the worth itself named as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都围绕「价值」：某物对你有价值、你把这份价值用起来，以及把这份价值本身当名词来称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: whether the strength in your hand actually counts for anything
core.cn: 核心意象：手里那点力气到底顶不顶用

branches.en: Protests that failed against a decision.
A resident taking up a grant.
Pleading that was of no use.
Both measure how much the effort was worth.
branches.cn: 两者都在衡量这份努力值多少。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail; the val root builds value, valid, prevail and equivalent.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail；val 词根构成 value、valid、prevail 与 equivalent。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is valere, to be strong, and valor, worth; the -able ending turns it into available.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 valere「强健」与 valor「价值」；加上 -able 词尾便成 available。

definition_zh: 可用性；可获得性；有货；空闲；可用人力；有效性（古义）；可用量；系统可用性；可得性
definition_en: the quality of being usable, obtainable, or free to be called on, whether of a thing, a resource, or a person
core_image: 仓库的门半开，架上还剩最后一箱；有人问的不是它好不好，而是现在能不能拿到
scene: 护士长查看病房白板，说床位是有的，真正卡住的是人手能不能排得出来。A nurse checks the ward board and says: We have the beds, but staff availability is the real limit.
sceneCN: 这里 availability 指「可用人力、到岗情况」（第 5 个义项：人员能否被调用）；句意：我们有床位，但真正受限的是可到岗的医护人员。画面里有病房白板、排班表和一支马克笔。

pos.zh: 可用性；可获得性；空闲；可用量

collocations.zh: 人员可用情况；到岗情况

derivatives.zh: 可用的；可获得的；有空的

senses.title: Fit to be used
senses.definition: the quality of being ready and fit to be used
senses.definitionCN: 处于可被使用的状态或性质
senses.example: The availability of clean water decides where the village is built.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁水源的可用性决定了村庄建在哪里。
senses.why: avail comes from a- 'to' + Latin valere 'be strong, be worth'; -able says 'capable of', and -ity names that capacity. A thing is available when it has the strength to be of use.
senses.whyCN: avail 出自 a-「向」+ 拉丁语 valere「强、有价值」；-able 表示「能够」，-ity 命名这种能力。一样东西可用，就是它有「能被用上」的那股力量。

senses.title: Obtainable when needed
senses.titleCN: 可获得性：需要时能弄到
senses.definition: the state of being obtainable when it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 在需要时能够获得的状态
senses.example: The availability of cheap flights changed the way people travel.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价航班的可获得性改变了人们的出行方式。
senses.why: The modern sense is recorded from 1827 for available, 'at one's disposal'. Availability generalizes it: not merely usable in principle, but findable in the market or in the system.
senses.whyCN: available 的现代义「可支配」记录于 1827 年。availability 把它一般化：不只是原则上能用，而是在市场或系统里找得到。

senses.title: On the shelf
senses.definition: the state of being in stock or on sale
senses.definitionCN: 有现货或正在出售的状态
senses.example: Tickets are sold on a first-come basis, subject to availability.
senses.exampleCN: 门票先到先得，视供应情况而定。
senses.why: Commerce narrowed the mass noun to stock on hand. The old sense of 'worth' survives faintly: what is on the shelf is what can be turned to account.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个不可数名词收窄为「手头现货」。旧义「有价值」还隐约残留：架上的东西才是能派上用场的东西。

senses.title: Free time in a diary
senses.definition: the free time a person has for a meeting or a task
senses.definitionCN: 一个人可用于会议或任务的空间时间
senses.example: The doctor's availability is limited to Tuesday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 这位医生的空闲时间仅限于周二上午。
senses.why: A person, like a resource, can be 'at disposal'. Scheduling language turns the abstract quality into a block of time that can be booked.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像资源一样「供支配」。排期语言把这种抽象性质变成一段可以被预订的时间。

senses.title: Hands that can be called on
senses.definition: the extent to which staff are present and able to work
senses.definitionCN: 员工到岗并能工作的程度
senses.example: Staff availability falls sharply during the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 收割期间，可用人力急剧下降。
senses.why: From 'at disposal' the word moves to the labour pool: who can be called on. The measure is human, but the metaphor is still that of a reserve.
senses.whyCN: 从「供支配」出发，这个词转向劳动力储备：谁叫得应。被衡量的是人，但比喻仍是「有一份储备」。

senses.title: Power to help, in older use
senses.definition: the power to produce a beneficial effect; efficacy, in older use
senses.definitionCN: 产生有益效果的力量；效力（旧义）
senses.example: The pamphlet promised the availability of the new remedy against fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子宣称这种新药对退烧有效。
senses.why: The 1803 sense was 'capability of advantageous use', closer to avail's original 'be of worth'. The word then meant usefulness, not presence on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 1803 年的义项是「可供有利使用的性能」，更接近 avail 最初的「有价值」。当时这个词指「有用」，而不是「架上有货」。

senses.title: How much can be drawn
senses.definition: the amount of a resource, especially water, that can be drawn on
senses.definitionCN: 可动用的资源量，尤指水量
senses.example: Climate change is reducing water availability in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化正在减少该地区的可用水量。
senses.why: Environmental science quantifies the old 'at disposal' idea. Availability becomes a measured volume: what the system can yield without being exhausted.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把古老的「供支配」观念量化。availability 变成一个有单位体积：系统在不被耗尽的前提下能产出多少。

senses.title: Uptime
senses.definition: the proportion of time a system is working and accessible
senses.definitionCN: 系统正常工作并可访问的时间比例
senses.example: The engineers promised 99.9 percent availability for the service.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师承诺这项服务的可用性达到 99.9%。
senses.why: Computing measures the same capacity as a percentage of time. A system is available when it can answer a request, which is valere 'be strong' translated into uptime.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域把同一种能力换算成时间百分比。系统能应答请求就是 available，也就是 valere「强」被翻译成了正常运行时间。

senses.title: What comes to mind
senses.definition: the ease with which examples come to mind, used as a mental shortcut in judging frequency
senses.definitionCN: 例子在脑中浮现的容易程度，被用作判断频率的心理捷径
senses.example: The availability heuristic makes rare crashes feel common after one is reported.
senses.exampleCN: 可得性启发让罕见的坠机在报道一起之后显得很常见。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for what is mentally 'at hand'. What comes easily to memory is judged frequent; the metaphor of a store one can draw from is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词指「在脑子里随手可及」的东西。容易想起的就被判断为常见；「有一份储备可抽取」的比喻原封未动。

intro.en: Availability is the abstract noun of available, a word built from avail, 'to be of worth'. Latin valere 'to be strong, be worth' is the muscle in it; -able makes 'capable of being used', and -ity turns that capacity into a measurable quality.
intro.cn: availability 是 available 的抽象名词，而 available 由 avail「有价值、有用」构成。里面的筋骨是拉丁语 valere「强、有价值」；-able 造出「能够被使用」，-ity 再把这种能力变成可测量的性质。

items.en: The root *wal- 'to be strong' is reconstructed from Latin valere and its relatives. There is no written record of this layer, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *wal-「强健」是从拉丁语 valere 及其亲属语重构出来的。这一层没有书面记录，因此标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: valere meant 'be strong, be well, be worth'; it also gave validus 'strong' (whence valid), valor and the verb praevalere 'prevail'. Worth and strength were one idea.
items.cn: valere 意为「强健、安好、有价值」；它还给出 validus「强壮的」（即 valid 的来源）、valor，以及动词 praevalere「占优势」。价值与力量在当时是一个概念。

items.en: avail is an Anglo-French compound of a- 'to' + the present stem vaill- of Old French valoir 'be worth', hence 'help, be profitable to, have force'.
items.cn: avail 是英法语的复合词，由 a-「向」+ 古法语 valoir「有价值」的现在时词干 vaill- 构成，意为「帮助、对……有利、有力量」。

items.en: available is recorded as 'beneficial' and 'valid, effective, capable of producing the desired effect', from avail + -able. The date usually cited is the middle of the 15th century.
items.cn: available 被记录为「有益的」和「有效的、能产生预期效果的」，由 avail + -able 构成。通常引用的年代是 15 世纪中叶。

items.en: availability appears as 'capability of advantageous use', from available + -ity. It still meant usefulness rather than presence.
items.cn: availability 以「可供有利使用的性能」出现，由 available + -ity 构成。当时它仍指有用性，而非「在场」。

items.en: available took the sense 'at one's disposal, capable of being made use of' in 1827; availability followed into stock, staff time, water, system uptime and, in the 1970s, the availability heuristic.
items.cn: available 于 1827 年获得「可支配、可利用」义；availability 随之进入库存、人员时间、水量、系统正常运行时间，并在 20 世纪 70 年代进入「可得性启发」。

note.en: The first group shares the avail- stem or the -ability ending; the second group names other kinds of access, supply, or readiness that availability can imply.
note.cn: 第一组共享 avail- 词干或 -ability 词尾；第二组是 availability 可能蕴含的其他「可接近、可供应、已就绪」的说法。

entries.definition: usable, obtainable, or free. It is avail + -able, the base of availability.
entries.definitionCN: 可用的；可获得的；有空的。它是 avail + -able，是 availability 的基础词。

entries.definition: not usable, not obtainable, or not free.
entries.definitionCN: 不可用的；无法获得的；没空的。

entries.definition: the state of not being available. It is the direct opposite of availability.
entries.definitionCN: 不可用；无法获得。它是 availability 的直接反义词。

entries.definition: to be of use or benefit; also benefit itself. The whole family grows from this root.
entries.definitionCN: 有用；有益；益处。整个词族都从这个词根长出来。

entries.definition: the quality of being easy to reach, enter, or use. It stresses the path to the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 可接近性；无障碍性。它强调通向事物之路。

entries.definition: the quality of being reachable as a goal. It stresses effort rather than supply.
entries.definitionCN: 可达性；可实现性。它强调努力，而非供应。

entries.definition: the state of being present in a place or situation. It is the plain fact behind one kind of availability.
entries.definitionCN: 在场；存在。它是某一类 availability 背后的朴素事实。

entries.definition: the amount of something provided or in stock. It is the quantity side of availability.
entries.definitionCN: 供应量；库存。它是 availability 的数量面。

entries.definition: the state of being prepared and fit for use or action.

normalIntro.en: avail is 'be of worth'; -able is 'can be'; -ity is 'the quality of'. So availability is literally 'the quality of being able to be of worth'.
normalIntro.cn: avail 是「有价值、有用」；-able 是「能够」；-ity 是「……的性质」。所以 availability 字面就是「能够派上用场的性质」。

normal.en: available + -ity: the adjective of 'can be used' becomes the noun of 'can be used'.
normal.cn: available + -ity：「能用的」形容词，变成「可用性」名词。

normal.en: Same ending as ability: if it is available, it has the ability to be used.
normal.cn: 和 ability 同样的词尾：东西 available，就是有「被使用的能力」。

normal.en: subject to availability means 'if there is any left on the shelf'.
normal.cn: subject to availability 的意思就是「架上还有的话」。

normal.en: A doctor's availability is not a shelf but a blank space in a diary.
normal.cn: 医生的 availability 不是货架，而是日程表上的一块空白。

normal.en: Water availability, system availability, staff availability: one word follows the resource wherever it is.
normal.cn: 可用水量、系统可用性、人员可用情况：资源走到哪，这个词就跟到哪。

abstract.en: Availability always asks a second question: not 'does it exist?' but 'can it be reached now, by this person, for this purpose?'
abstract.cn: availability 总要追问第二层：不是「它存在吗」，而是「现在、这个人、为这个用途，能不能拿到？」

abstract.en: The word carries strength in its root: usable things are the ones with enough force to be turned to account.
abstract.cn: 这个词的词根里带着力量：能用的东西，才有足够的力量被派上用场。

abstract.en: From a shelf to a diary to a memory: the same word measures how close a thing is to the hand.
abstract.cn: 从货架到日程表再到记忆：同一个词测量的都是「东西离手有多近」。

examples.en: The availability of parts delayed the repair by a week.
examples.cn: 零件的可获得性让维修推迟了一周。

examples.en: Please confirm your availability for the meeting on Friday.
examples.cn: 请确认你周五能否出席会议。

examples.en: The study links low water availability to migration.
examples.cn: 这项研究把可用水量低与人口迁移联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: a（一个）+ vail（围栏，vale）+ ability（能力）——围栏里还剩一个，有「能拿到」的能力 → availability 可用性；可获得性

root: 源自 avail「有价值、有用」+ -able「能够」+ -ity「性质」；avail 出自 a-（ad-「向」）+ 拉丁语 valere「强、有价值」，核心是「有力量、能被派上用场」，再引申为「可拿到、可支配」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses ask the same practical question in different places: a shelf, a diary, a ward, a reservoir, a server, a memory. In each, availability measures how close the thing is to being used.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同场所问同一个实际问题：货架、日程表、病房、水库、服务器、记忆。每个场景里，availability 都在衡量「这东西离被使用有多近」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a thing that is there and free to be taken.
core.cn: 核心意象：手伸向一样就在那里、可以拿走的东西。

branches.en: CAPACITY TO HELP: fit for use, and the older sense of efficacy or worth.
branches.cn: 能帮上忙：适合使用，以及较旧的「有效、有价值」义。

branches.en: OBTAINABLE: findable when needed, and actually in stock.
branches.cn: 能拿到：需要时找得到，以及确实有现货。

branches.en: PEOPLE AT DISPOSAL: free time in a diary and hands that can be called on.
branches.cn: 可供支配的人：日程表上的空档，以及叫得应的人手。

branches.en: MEASURED RESOURCES: a volume of water and a percentage of uptime.
branches.cn: 被测量的资源：可用水量与正常运行时间百分比。

branches.en: AT HAND IN THE MIND: what comes easily to memory and is judged frequent.
branches.cn: 脑中随手可及：容易想起、因而被判断为常见的东西。

intro.en: availability is avail + -able + -ity. avail is a- (ad-, 'to') + val- (Latin valere, 'be strong, be worth'); -able makes 'capable of', -ity makes the quality noun. The negative uses un- twice: unavailable, unavailability.
intro.cn: availability 是 avail + -able + -ity。avail 为 a-（ad-「向」）+ val-（拉丁语 valere「强、有价值」）；-able 造「能够」，-ity 造性质名词。否定式两次用 un-：unavailable、unavailability。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere 'be strong, be worth' yields validus 'strong' (valid), valor, and praevalere 'prevail'; the -abilis suffix behind -able marks capability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere「强、有价值」给出 validus「强壮的」（即 valid）、valor，以及 praevalere「占优势」；-able 背后的 -abilis 后缀标记「能够」。

items.meaning: the quality of being usable or obtainable
items.example: The availability of the drug varies by region.
items.exampleCN: 这种药的可获得性因地区而异。

items.meaning: to be of use or benefit
items.example: All their efforts availed them nothing.
items.exampleCN: 他们的一切努力都无济于事。

items.meaningCN: 可用的；可获得的；有空的
items.example: Tickets are available at the door.
The manager is unavailable until Monday.

items.meaning: the state of not being available
items.example: The unavailability of parts stopped production.
items.exampleCN: 零件无法获得，生产因此停顿。

items.example: The old word availment meant a profit gained.
items.exampleCN: 古词 availment 指获得的益处。

items.meaning: sound, legally effective, or logically strong
items.meaningCN: 有效的；正当的；有根据的
items.example: The passport is valid for ten years.

items.meaning: the quality of being sound or legally effective
items.example: The court questioned the validity of the contract.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑这份合同的有效性。

items.meaning: worth, or the importance of something
items.example: The value of the land has doubled.
items.exampleCN: 这块地的价值翻了一番。

items.meaning: to win out or be widespread
items.example: Cooler weather prevailed after the storm.

latinEntries.meaning: to be strong, be well, be worth

definition_zh: 可获得的，可用的；有空的；有效的（票、座位等仍可购买）
definition_en: able to be obtained or used, free to see someone, or still open to be bought
core_image: 货架上还留着一件，手伸过去就能拿到
scene: 订票页面刷新了一下，原本灰掉的座位重新亮起。Two seats are still available.
sceneCN: 这里 available 是「可获得的、可用的」（第 1 个义项：还能拿到）；句意是还有两个座位可选。

pos.zh: 形容词：可获得的；有空的；有效的

derivatives.zh: 形容词：不可获得的；没空的

senses.title: Able to be had
senses.definition: able to be obtained, bought or used
senses.definitionCN: 能够被取得、买到或使用的
senses.example: Two seats are still available.
senses.exampleCN: 还有两个座位可选。
senses.why: The word is built on avail, 'to be of use or worth', so available describes something that is there and can be put to use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 avail「有用、有价值」之上，所以 available 描述的是东西就在那里、可以拿来用。

senses.title: Free to meet
senses.definition: not busy, and therefore free to meet or talk
senses.definitionCN: 不忙，因此可以见面或交谈
senses.example: The doctor is available after three.
senses.exampleCN: 医生三点以后有空。
senses.why: A person, like a thing, can be on hand and ready to be used; here the use is someone's time rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 人像物品一样，可以在手边、随时可用；只是这里的「用」指的是对方的时间，而不是物件。

senses.title: Still open to buy
senses.definition: not yet sold or booked, and therefore still open to customers
senses.definitionCN: 尚未售出或订走，因此仍向顾客开放
senses.example: The ticket is available until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票在周五之前都能买。
senses.why: In ticketing the word narrows to stock that has not been taken, which is why it so often appears beside seats and rooms.
senses.whyCN: 在售票语境里，这个词收窄为「还没被拿走的名额」，所以常与座位、房间一起出现。

intro.en: Available grows from an old verb meaning to be of worth or use.
intro.cn: available 来自一个古老动词，意为「有价值、有用处」。

items.en: valere meant 'to be strong or be worth'.
items.cn: valere 意为「有力量、有价值」。

items.en: valoir meant 'to be worth'.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 意为「值、有用」。

items.en: availer meant 'to be of use or help'.
items.cn: 古法语 availer 意为「有用、有帮助」。

items.en: English avail kept the sense of being useful.
items.cn: 英语 avail 保留了「有用」的意思。

items.en: The adjective named what can be used or obtained.
items.cn: 形容词形式指可以被使用或取得的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the avail root; the near-meaning group gives words for reachable things and free time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 avail 词根；近义组是表示可得之物与空闲时间的词。

normalIntro.en: Available says something or someone is there and can be used.
normalIntro.cn: available 表示某物或某人在那里、可以用得上。

normal.en: The base is avail, to be of use, plus -able, able to.
normal.cn: 词基是 avail「有用」，加 -able「能够」。

normal.en: Available to names who may use it; available for names the purpose.
normal.cn: available to 引出可以使用的人，available for 引出用途。

normal.en: For people it means not busy, as in the doctor is available.
normal.cn: 用于人时表示不忙，例如医生有空。

normal.en: Readily available means easy to get, not merely existing.
normal.cn: readily available 表示容易得到，不只是存在。

normal.en: Unavailable adds un- and means the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 un- 构成 unavailable，意思相反。

abstract.en: See one last item still sitting on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上还剩下最后一件。

abstract.en: See a grey seat turn green on a booking screen.
abstract.cn: 想象订票屏幕上灰色座位变成绿色。

abstract.en: See an open door and a free chair in an office.
abstract.cn: 想象办公室门开着，椅子空着。

examples.en: Two seats are still available.
examples.cn: 还有两个座位可选。

examples.en: The doctor is available after three.
examples.cn: 医生三点以后有空。

examples.en: The ticket is available until Friday.
examples.cn: 这张票在周五之前都能买。

dict_mnemonic.text: avail（有用）加 -able（能够）：东西能拿到、能用上是可获得的，人的时间能用上是 有空的，票还没卖完是仍可购买的。

root: 源自中古英语 avail「有用、有价值」，更早来自古法语 availer 与拉丁语 valere「有力量、有价值」；加形容词词尾 -able 后表示「可以被取得或使用」，再由物及人，引申为「有空」。

sensesIntro.en: A product, a person's time and an unsold ticket can all be available.
sensesIntro.cn: 一件商品、一个人的时间、一张没卖出的票，都可以是 available。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last item on the shelf within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架上还剩一件，伸手可及。

intro.en: The root avail, 'to be of use', takes -able to make available.
intro.cn: 词根 avail 意为「有用」，加 -able 构成 available。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, 'to be worth', also gives value, valid and evaluate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere「有价值」也是 value、valid 与 evaluate 的来源。

items.meaning: able to be used or had

definition_zh: 雪崩；山崩；大量涌现之物；纷至沓来
definition_en: a mass of snow, ice, or rock sliding swiftly down a mountainside; also, an overwhelming quantity of things arriving at once
core_image: 山坡上的积雪突然整体松脱，轰然压向谷底
scene: 向导忽然吹响哨子，整面山坡的积雪开始滑动。An avalanche buried the trail behind the climbers.
sceneCN: 这里 avalanche 指「雪崩」（第 1 个义项：积雪滑落）；句意：雪崩掩埋了登山者身后的路径。

pos.zh: 雪崩；崩塌；大量涌来之物
雪崩般涌下；压倒性地到来

derivatives.zh: 板状雪崩（复合术语，最危险的类型）
山体滑坡（近义构造，另一词根）

senses.title: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain
senses.definition: a large mass of snow and ice that slides swiftly down a mountainside
senses.definitionCN: 大量积雪沿山坡急速滑落的灾害
senses.example: The avalanche cut off the only road into the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 雪崩切断了进谷的唯一道路。
senses.why: The core image is a slope letting go: once the snow starts moving, nothing can hold it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是山坡松手：积雪一旦开始滑动，什么都拦不住。

senses.title: A fall of rock or earth
senses.definition: a similar slide of rock, soil, or debris down a slope
senses.definitionCN: 岩石、泥土或碎屑沿坡面发生的类似滑落
senses.example: A rock avalanche blocked the river and formed a lake.
senses.exampleCN: 岩崩堵塞河道，形成了一片湖泊。
senses.why: Any loose mass on a slope shares the snowslide's logic, so the word extended.
senses.whyCN: 坡上任何松散物都具有雪崩式的滑动逻辑，词义随之扩展。

senses.title: An overwhelming quantity arriving at once
senses.titleCN: 大量涌现之物；纷至沓来
senses.definition: an overwhelmingly large amount of something arriving together
senses.definitionCN: 同时涌来的压倒性数量的事物
senses.example: The show received an avalanche of fan mail.
senses.exampleCN: 节目组收到雪片般的观众来信。
senses.why: The mass-on-the-move image fits anything that arrives all at once and cannot be stopped.
senses.whyCN: 「整体滑动、无法阻挡」的意象正好形容同时涌来、无从招架的大量事物。

senses.title: A sudden breakdown of a system
senses.definition: a rapid chain reaction in which one failure triggers many others
senses.definitionCN: 一处失灵引发接连崩溃的连锁反应
senses.example: A small outage caused an avalanche of server failures.
senses.exampleCN: 一次小故障引发了服务器接连崩溃。
senses.why: Physics borrows the slope image: one slipping grain sets the whole pile moving.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用坡面意象：一粒沙滑动，整个沙堆随之而动。

senses.title: To descend like an avalanche
senses.definition: to move down or forward in a sudden, irresistible mass
senses.definitionCN: 如雪崩般以不可阻挡的整体之势涌下
senses.example: Runners avalanched down the final hill of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 选手们在赛道最后一坡一拥而下。
senses.why: The noun turned verb keeps the single picture: the whole mass moving at once.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词保留了同一画面：整体同时移动。

senses.title: To overwhelm completely
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with far more than can be handled
senses.definitionCN: 以远超承受能力的事物将人压倒
senses.example: The interns were avalanched with paperwork on day one.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生们第一天就被文书工作淹没。
senses.why: Being under an avalanche means being buried; the verb keeps the burial.
senses.whyCN: 身处雪崩即被掩埋，动词保留了这个「被埋」义。

senses.title: In electronics, a self-sustaining cascade
senses.definition: of current or particles, a multiplying cascade, as in avalanche breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 指电流或粒子自我倍增的级联，如雪崩击穿
senses.example: Avalanche diodes exploit a controlled electron cascade.
senses.exampleCN: 雪崩二极管利用受控的电子级联。
senses.why: One carrier frees two, two free four: growth that mimics the snowslide.
senses.whyCN: 一个载流子撞出两个、两个撞出四个：增长方式与雪崩如出一辙。

senses.title: In sports, a sudden cascade of scoring
senses.definition: a rapid run of goals or points against one side
senses.definitionCN: 一方接连失分或对方连续得分的局面
senses.example: Three goals in ten minutes started an avalanche.
senses.exampleCN: 十分钟内连进三球，攻势如雪崩般展开。
senses.why: Once the first goal falls, more seem to follow by the same slope logic.
senses.whyCN: 第一球失守后，失球便如顺坡而下般接连发生。

intro.en: Avalanche comes from French avalanche, from a Savoyard patois word for a snowslide, probably built on the verb avaler, to descend, from Latin ad plus vallum, valley; the deeper prehistory is uncertain.
intro.cn: avalanche 出自法语 avalanche，源于萨瓦地区方言中「雪滑」一词，一般认为由动词 avaler「落下」构成，后者出自拉丁语 ad（向）+ vallum（谷）；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Late Latin had a term for descent or landslide, traditionally linked to ad, toward, plus vallum, valley.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语已有指下落或滑坡的词，传统上联系 ad「向」+ vallum「谷」。

items.en: Savoyard shepherds used lavanche or avalantze for a snow that slides.
items.cn: 萨瓦牧人用 lavanche、avalantze 一类词指会滑动的雪。

items.en: Standard French fixed the form avalanche for the Alpine snowslide.
items.cn: 标准法语在 17 至 18 世纪固定为 avalanche，指阿尔卑斯雪崩。

items.en: English travelers in the Alps borrowed the word; Horace Walpole helped popularize it.
items.cn: 游历阿尔卑斯的英国人借入该词，沃波尔等人使其流行。

items.en: The figurative sense, an overwhelming flood of things, spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 19 世纪，「大量涌来」的比喻义广泛传播。

items.en: Physics and electronics adopted the word for multiplying cascades.
items.cn: 物理学与电子学借该词命名自我倍增的级联现象。

note.en: Group one gathers look-alikes and borrowed French relatives; group two gathers other words for slides and floods.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词及法语借词近亲；第二组收其他滑坡、倾泻类词。

entries.definition: relating to bonds that pay yearly interest; shares only the opening letters.
entries.definitionCN: 按年付息的（债券）；仅开头字母与 avalanche 相同，词源无关。

entries.definition: washing out of a body cavity; ends in a similar -age sound but has no Alpine past.
entries.definitionCN: 灌洗术；词尾读音相近，但与雪山毫无渊源，词源不同。

entries.definition: the French verb to swallow or let down, inside the word's probable history.
entries.definitionCN: 法语动词「吞下、放下」，一般认为藏在本词的构成史中。

entries.definition: a slide of earth or rock; also a sweeping electoral victory.
entries.definitionCN: 山体滑坡；也指压倒性的选举胜利。

entries.definition: a violent stream, literal or of words.
entries.definitionCN: 急流；也指倾泻般的话语。

entries.definition: a great flood; an overwhelming amount arriving together.
entries.definitionCN: 大洪水；同时涌来的大量事物。

entries.definition: a small waterfall; a sequence in which each step triggers the next.
entries.definitionCN: 小瀑布；层层引发的连锁序列。

normalIntro.en: Read avalanche as a-val-anch: a mass anchoring loose, then sliding down the valley.
normalIntro.cn: 把 avalanche 拆成 a-val-anch 记：松脱的雪团顺谷而下。

normal.en: val inside the word echoes Latin vallum, valley: snow runs down into the valley.
normal.cn: 词中 val 呼应拉丁语 vallum「谷」：雪往谷底滑。

normal.en: French avaler means to swallow: the mountain swallows the village.
normal.cn: 法语 avaler 意为吞下：大山吞掉村庄。

normal.en: an avalanche of is the fixed figurative pattern.
normal.cn: an avalanche of 是固定比喻搭配：大量的。

normal.en: trigger and avalanche often go together in news English.
normal.cn: 新闻英语中 trigger 与 avalanche 常连用：引发雪崩。

normal.en: Plural spelling: avalanche ends -che, so the s stays audible.
normal.cn: 复数拼写：词尾 -che，加 s 后仍发 /ʃ/ 音。

abstract.en: Hear one crack, then the whole slope answering.
abstract.cn: 先听一声脆响，接着整面山坡回应。

abstract.en: Picture your inbox buried to the ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象你的收件箱被信件埋到天花板。

abstract.en: Avalanche is gravity losing patience in one piece.
abstract.cn: 雪崩是重力在一瞬间整体失去耐心。

examples.en: Rescue teams probed the snow for hours after the avalanche.
examples.cn: 雪崩后救援队在雪中探测了数小时。

examples.en: The report triggered an avalanche of complaints from readers.
examples.cn: 报道引发读者铺天盖地的投诉。

examples.en: Skiers carry beacons in case they are avalanched off the piste.
examples.cn: 滑雪者携带信标，以防在雪道外遭遇雪崩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿瓦，愣失」——阿瓦还愣着，雪已失滑而下，轰隆隆追了上来

root: 出自法语 avalanche，源于萨瓦方言指雪滑的词；一般认为由晚期拉丁语指下落的词构成，常见分析为 ad（向）+ vallum（谷），即「向谷中落下」；更早来源不确定。18 世纪经阿尔卑斯旅行文学进入英语，词形与法语一致。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the literal snowslide outward: rockfalls, floods of mail, chain-reaction failures, and the verb meanings built on the same mass-in-motion picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的雪崩向外延展：岩崩、信件洪流、连锁崩塌，以及由「整体运动」画面派生的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole slope of snow letting go at once, moving as one mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：整面山坡的积雪同时松脱，作为一个整体移动。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SIDE: snowslides and rockslides on real slopes.
branches.cn: 自然一面：真实坡面上的雪崩与岩崩。

branches.en: THE QUANTITY SIDE: mail, applications, praise arriving as one mass.
branches.cn: 数量一面：信件、申请、赞誉一齐涌到。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM SIDE: failures and particles multiplying down the chain.
branches.cn: 系统一面：故障与粒子沿链条倍增。

branches.en: THE VERB SIDE: to move or bury with that same mass force.
branches.cn: 动词一面：以同样的整体之力涌动或掩埋。

branches.en: THE SPORTS SIDE: goals falling faster than a defense can hold.
branches.cn: 体育一面：失球快过防线所能承受。

intro.en: Avalanche is a folk-split word: speakers long read it as a French verb phrase a valer, to descend, so no clean prefix plus root division survives.
intro.cn: avalanche 常被民间拆解为法语动词短语 a valer「落下」，因此没有干净的前缀加词根分界。

latinIntro.en: The Latin trace is the pair ad, toward, and vallum, valley, behind the later French verb avaler.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁痕迹在于 ad（向）与 vallum（谷）这对成分，后融入法语动词 avaler。

items.meaning: marker of the dialect word lavanche

definition_zh: v. 为（他人或自己所受的伤害）报仇；替……复仇
definition_en: To inflict punishment in return for a wrong done to oneself or to another person.
core_image: 替倒下的人把那一击还回去
scene: 他发誓要替被害的兄弟报仇。He swore to avenge his murdered brother.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：avenge 指为他人所受的伤害而施加惩罚，宾语通常是受害者或那桩伤害。

senses.title: Punish a wrong for someone
senses.titleCN: 替他人所受的伤害施加惩罚
senses.definition: to take or exact punishment for a harm suffered by another person or by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 为他人或自己所受的伤害而施加或索取惩罚
senses.example: They raised an army to avenge the raid.
senses.exampleCN: 他们集结军队为那次袭击复仇。
senses.why: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Latin vindicare, to claim or punish, so it directs a claim of justice at a wrong.
senses.whyCN: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，因此它把一份正义诉求指向那桩伤害。

senses.title: Reflexive retaliation
senses.definition: in a reflexive pattern with on, to pay back a personal injury by harming the offender
senses.definitionCN: 用于带 on 的反身句式，指以伤害冒犯者来回报自身所受的损害
senses.example: He avenged himself on the men who cheated him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那些骗过他的人复仇。
senses.why: The reflexive keeps the injured party in view, which is what separates avenge from revenge in careful use.
senses.whyCN: 反身式让受害者始终在视野之中，这正是严谨用法中 avenge 与 revenge 的分界。

intro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Old French avengier, from Latin vindicare, to lay claim to or punish, from vindex, a claimant or avenger.
intro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自古法语 avengier，源自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，而 vindicare 出自 vindex「索求者、复仇者」。

items.en: A root meaning to point out or claim stands behind words of showing and demanding.
items.cn: 一个表示「指出、索求」的词根支撑着显示与要求类的词。

items.en: Latin vindex named a claimant, one who demands a thing back or answers for a wrong.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vindex 指索求者，即索回某物或为不公讨回公道的人。

items.en: From it vindicare meant to lay claim to, to set free, and to punish.
items.cn: 由此 vindicare 意为「索还、释放、惩罚」。

items.en: Old French venger kept the punishing side, to take vengeance for a harm.
items.cn: 古法语 venger 保留了惩罚一面，即为伤害复仇。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave avengier, to direct that punishment at a wrong.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avengier，即把惩罚指向某桩伤害。

items.en: Middle English avengen entered in the fourteenth century and displaced older native words.
items.cn: 中古英语 avengen 于十四世纪进入，取代了更早的本族词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the venge family; the near-meaning group lists other words for paying back a wrong.
note.cn: 形近组保留 venge 词族；近义组列出其他表示回报伤害的词。

entries.definition: The place where an event is held.
To answer an attack with an attack.
To repay a good or an evil.
To impose a penalty for a wrong.

normalIntro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge, kin to vengeance: aim the payback at a wrong done to someone.
normalIntro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，与 vengeance 同族：把回报瞄准某人所受的伤害。

normal.en: Avenge takes the victim or the wrong as object.
normal.cn: avenge 的宾语是受害者或那桩伤害。

normal.en: Revenge is usually personal; avenge is for justice.
normal.cn: revenge 多出于私怨，avenge 多为公道。

normal.en: The reflexive pattern ends with on plus a person.
normal.cn: 反身句式以 on 加某人收尾。

normal.en: The noun is vengeance, the person is avenger.
normal.cn: 名词是 vengeance，人是 avenger。

normal.en: Vindicate shares the root but means to clear.
normal.cn: vindicate 同根，但意为洗清。

abstract.en: Picture a blow returned for a fallen friend.
abstract.cn: 想象为倒下的朋友还回那一击。

abstract.en: Imagine scales tipped back into balance.
abstract.cn: 想象天平被重新扳回平衡。

abstract.en: Think of a debt of pain being settled.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔痛苦的债被结清。

examples.en: The son avenged his father in court.
examples.cn: 儿子在法庭上为父亲讨回公道。

examples.en: She avenged herself on her old employer.
examples.cn: 她向旧雇主复了仇。

examples.en: Nothing could avenge such a loss.
examples.cn: 任何事都无法为这样的损失复仇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ venge（与 vengeance 同族，「报复」）——把报复指向那桩伤害，就是 avenge。

root: 拉丁语 vindex「索求者」生出 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，古法语 venger 加 a-「向」成 avengier，入中古英语作 avengen，即 avenge「为……复仇」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses aim punishment at a wrong: for another person or oneself, and in the reflexive pattern against the offender.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都把惩罚指向一桩伤害：为他人或自己所受的伤害，以及在反身句式中指向冒犯者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: returning the blow on behalf of the one who fell
core.cn: 核心意象：替倒下的人把那一击还回去

branches.en: An army raised for a raid.
branches.cn: 为一次袭击集结的军队。

branches.en: A son answering for his father.
branches.cn: 为父亲讨回公道的儿子。

branches.en: A worker settling with an old employer.
Both treat the wrong as a debt.
branches.cn: 两者都把伤害当作一笔债。

intro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge; the vind root builds vengeance, revenge, vindicate and vengeful.
intro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge；vind 词根构成 vengeance、revenge、vindicate 与 vengeful。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is vindex, a claimant, and vindicare, to claim or punish; poena, penalty, gives punish beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 vindex「索求者」与 vindicare「索还、惩罚」；旁边的 poena「刑罚」产生 punish。

definition_zh: 大街；林荫道；途径
definition_en: a wide street in a town, or a way of reaching a goal
core_image: 两侧栽满树的宽阔街道，一直通向前方
scene: 清晨的街道很安静。A wide avenue runs from the station to the park.
sceneCN: 这里 avenue 是「大街」（第 1 个义项：城市里的宽阔道路）；句意是一条宽阔的大街从车站一直通到公园。

derivatives.zh: 同源词，con-（共同）加 venire（来），义为「召集；集会」
同源词，inter-（之间）加 venire（来），义为「介入；干预」
同源词，ad-（向）加 venire（来），义为「到来；出现」

senses.title: A wide street
senses.definition: a wide street in a town, often lined with trees
senses.definitionCN: 城市中宽阔的街道，两侧常栽有树木
senses.example: A wide avenue runs from the station to the park.
senses.exampleCN: 一条宽阔的大街从车站一直通到公园。
senses.why: Avenue comes from French avenue, a way of approach, from Latin advenire, to come to; the street sense grew from the idea of a route that leads you toward a place.
senses.whyCN: avenue 经法语 avenue「接近之路」来自拉丁语 advenire「来到」；街道义正是从「把人引向某处的通路」长出来的。

senses.title: A way to achieve something
senses.definition: a possible way of achieving something or dealing with a problem
senses.definitionCN: 达成某事或处理问题的可能方式
senses.example: The talks opened a new avenue for peace.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈为和平开辟了一条新途径。
senses.why: If a street is a route toward a place, then any route toward a result can be called an avenue, especially in formal writing about options.
senses.whyCN: 既然街道是通向某地的路线，那么通向结果的任何路线也能叫 avenue，正式文体里常用来指可选项。

intro.en: Avenue is a word about a way that leads you toward something.
intro.cn: avenue 说的是把人引向某处的一条路。

items.en: venire meant 'to come'.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」。

items.en: advenire meant 'to come to'.
items.cn: advenire 意为「来到」。

items.en: avenue meant 'a way of approach'.
items.cn: avenue 意为「接近之路」。

items.en: English avenue first named a road leading to a house.
items.cn: 英语 avenue 起初指通向宅邸的道路。

items.en: It came to mean any wide city street.
items.cn: 后来泛指城市里的宽阔街道。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long u ending; the near-meaning group gives streets and routes.
note.cn: 形近组都有长元音结尾；近义组是街道与路线的词。

entries.definition: money that a business or government receives
to punish someone for a wrong
a way from one place to another

normalIntro.en: An avenue is a broad way in, and later any broad way to a result.
normalIntro.cn: avenue 先是宽阔的进入之路，后指通向结果的宽路。

normal.en: Think of a road wide enough for two rows of trees.
normal.cn: 想象一条宽到能栽两排树的道路。

normal.en: The plural is avenues, with the stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 复数是 avenues，重音在第一音节。

normal.en: Avenue is common in street names such as Fifth Avenue.
normal.cn: avenue 常用于街道名，如第五大道。

normal.en: In formal English an avenue can be an option to explore.
normal.cn: 正式英语里 avenue 也可指可探索的途径。

normal.en: The final letters -ue are not pronounced as a separate syllable.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ue 不单独构成音节。

abstract.en: See a long straight road framed by two lines of trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一条笔直长路，两旁各有一排树。

abstract.en: See a map with one wide road cutting across many small ones.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一条大路横穿许多小路。

abstract.en: See a door opening at the end of that road.
abstract.cn: 想象那条路的尽头有一扇门打开。

examples.en: A wide avenue runs from the station to the park.
examples.cn: 一条宽阔的大街从车站一直通到公园。

examples.en: The talks opened a new avenue for peace.
examples.cn: 会谈为和平开辟了一条新途径。

examples.en: They explored every avenue before giving up.
examples.cn: 他们在放弃之前探索了各种途径。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（向）加 ven（来）加 -ue：一条把人「引向」某处的路，先是林荫大街，后引申为做事的途径。

root: 源自拉丁语 advenire「来到」，由 ad-「向」与 venire「来」构成，经古法语 avenue「接近之路」进入英语；由通往宅邸的道路引申为城市大街与做事途径。

sensesIntro.en: A street and a route to a result share one image of a way that leads somewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 街道与达成结果的途径，共享同一个「引向某处」的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broad way leading toward a place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条宽阔的路把人引向某处。

intro.en: The Latin root venire, 'to come', brings a family of arriving and approaching words into English.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 venire 意为「来」，为英语带来一批表示到来与接近的词。

latinIntro.en: Avenue is built on advenire, and the same base underlies many formal verbs.
latinIntro.cn: avenue 建在 advenire 之上，同一词基也构成许多正式动词。

items.meaning: a thing that comes to mind

definition_zh: 平均数；平均的；普通的；平均为
definition_en: the middle amount or level, or to amount to such a level
core_image: 一排高低不齐的柱子被一条水平线穿过
scene: 老师在讲台上翻开成绩册。The average score of the class rose this term.
sceneCN: 这里 average 是「平均数」（第 1 个义项：把总数按份数均分得到的值）；句意是这个班的平均分本学期提高了。

derivatives.zh: 由 average 加 -ly 构成，义为「平均地；普通地」
由 average 与 sized 复合而成，义为「中等大小的」

senses.title: The middle amount
senses.definition: the result of adding several amounts and dividing by their number
senses.definitionCN: 把若干数量相加后除以个数所得的结果
senses.example: The average of three, five and seven is five.
senses.exampleCN: 三、五、七的平均数是五。
senses.why: Average comes from French avarie, damage to goods at sea, because a shared loss was divided among merchants; the arithmetic sense grew from dividing a total fairly.
senses.whyCN: average 来自法语 avarie「海损」，因为共同损失要由商人分摊；算术上的「平均」正是从这种平摊长出来的。

senses.title: Typical or ordinary
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or unusual
senses.definitionCN: 普通而并无特别之处的
senses.example: She is an average student who works hard.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个努力用功的普通学生。
senses.why: If an average is the middle of a range, then a person or thing near that middle is ordinary, neither very good nor very bad.
senses.whyCN: 既然平均数是区间的中点，那么处在中点附近的人或物就是普通的，不算特别好也不算特别差。

senses.title: To amount to as a mean
senses.definition: to reach an average of a particular amount over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里达到某个平均数值
senses.example: Sales averaged two hundred units a month.
senses.exampleCN: 每月销量平均为两百件。
senses.why: The noun meaning the middle value turned into a verb meaning to produce that middle value over time.
senses.whyCN: 表示中间值的名词转成动词，就表示在一段时间里得出那个平均值。

intro.en: Average began as a word about shared loss at sea.
intro.cn: average 最初是一个讲海上共同损失的说法。

items.en: habere meant 'to have', the base of later French forms.
items.cn: habere 意为「有」，是后来法语词形的词基。

items.en: awariya meant damaged goods.
items.cn: awariya 意为受损的货物。

items.en: avarie meant damage to a ship or its cargo.
items.cn: avarie 意为船只或货物的损失。

items.en: averay meant a charge shared by merchants.
items.cn: averay 意为商人分摊的费用。

items.en: The word settled on the sense of a middle value.
items.cn: 这个词最后固定为「平均值」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group starts with a short a; the near-meaning group gives middle and ordinary words.
note.cn: 形近组都以短促的 a 起头；近义组是表示中间与普通的词。

the middle value of a set of numbers

normalIntro.en: Average turns uneven amounts into one flat level and then calls that level ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: average 把高低不齐的数量摊成一条水平线，再把这个水平称作普通。

normal.en: Average has three syllables, with the stress on the first.
normal.cn: average 有三个音节，重音在第一个。

normal.en: Use on average to speak about a general level.
normal.cn: 谈总体水平时用 on average。

normal.en: As a verb, average takes no preposition.
normal.cn: 作动词时 average 不加介词。

normal.en: Above average and below average mark the two sides.
normal.cn: 高于平均与低于平均分别标出两侧。

normal.en: Do not confuse average with avarice, which means greed.
normal.cn: 别把 average 与表示贪婪的 avarice 混淆。

abstract.en: See a row of uneven bars with one flat line through them.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高低不齐的柱子被一条水平线穿过。

abstract.en: See several cups of water poured into one wide jar.
abstract.cn: 想象几杯水倒进一只宽口罐里。

abstract.en: See a crowd where most heads reach the same height.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里大多数脑袋都一样高。

examples.en: The average score of the class rose this term.
examples.cn: 这个班的平均分本学期提高了。

examples.en: On average, the train arrives ten minutes late.
examples.cn: 平均而言，这趟火车晚点十分钟。

examples.en: Sales averaged two hundred units a month.
examples.cn: 每月销量平均为两百件。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ver 加 -age：把高低不齐的数摊平到同一条线上，就是平均数，也就是普普通通的水平。

root: 源自法语 avarie「海损」，上溯至意大利语 avaria，可能来自阿拉伯语 awariya「受损货物」；由商人平摊损失引申为「平均分担」，再固定为「平均数」。

sensesIntro.en: A fair share, a middle value and an ordinary level are one idea seen from three sides.
sensesIntro.cn: 平摊、中间值与普通水平，是同一个想法的三个侧面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat line cutting through uneven heights.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条水平线穿过高低不齐的柱子。

intro.en: The ending -age is a French noun marker, and average still behaves like a French borrowing.
intro.cn: 词尾 -age 是法语名词标记，average 至今仍像法语借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, 'to have', lies behind several French forms that shaped average.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere「有」藏在几个塑造 average 的法语词形之后。
