the act of carrying, or a vehicle

definition_zh: 反对的；厌恶的；不愿的
definition_en: having a strong dislike of or opposition to something
core_image: 身体往后一转，把脸从某物上挪开
scene: 父亲把菜推向桌子另一头。He was averse to any dish with cilantro.
sceneCN: 这里 averse 指「厌恶的、不愿的」（第 1 个义项：强烈反感）；句意：他讨厌任何加香菜的菜。

pos.zh: 厌恶的；反对的；不愿的（常作表语）

derivatives.zh: 厌恶；反感（averse + -ion 的名词化）
令人反感的（心理学用语，averse + -ive）

senses.title: Feeling strong dislike
senses.definition: feeling firm dislike or repugnance toward something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有坚定反感或厌恶
senses.example: She was averse to discussing salaries at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她反感在饭桌上谈工资。
senses.why: The Latin root means turned away: dislike as the body turning from a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「转开」：厌恶即身体从某物上转过去。

senses.title: Opposed in attitude
senses.definition: opposed to a proposal, practice, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 对提案、做法或行动路线持反对态度
senses.example: The board was averse to the merger from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会从一开始就反对这桩并购。
senses.why: Turning away extends from feelings to positions taken.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」从情绪延伸到所持立场。

senses.title: Unwilling to do something
senses.definition: reluctant or unwilling, as in not averse to helping
senses.definitionCN: 不情愿、不肯做，如 not averse to helping
senses.example: He is not averse to an extra shift when the pay doubles.
senses.exampleCN: 工资翻倍的话，他并不介意多加一个班。
senses.why: In the litotes not averse, the turning away is only mild.
senses.whyCN: 在低调说法 not averse 中，「转开」的程度很轻。

senses.title: Avoiding risk in economics
senses.definition: preferring certainty over gambles, as in risk-averse investors
senses.definitionCN: 宁取确定而回避赌博，如 risk-averse 投资者
senses.example: Risk-averse buyers chose the fixed-rate loan.
senses.exampleCN: 规避风险的买家选择了固定利率贷款。
senses.why: The turning-away image fits decision theory: turning from variance.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」意象契合决策论：从波动前转开身去。

senses.title: In psychology, producing avoidance
senses.definition: describing stimuli that organisms work to avoid, via the adjective aversive
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体极力回避的刺激，经由 aversive 一词
senses.example: Aversive shocks shaped the rats' learned avoidance.
senses.exampleCN: 厌恶电击塑造了大鼠习得的回避行为。
senses.why: The turning-away became a technical term for what drives it.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」变成了驱动回避行为的术语。

senses.title: Turned away in older English
senses.definition: in older or technical use, physically turned in a direction away from something
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或技术用法中，身体或器官背向某物
senses.example: Older botany texts described leaves averse to the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 旧植物学文献描述叶片背向茎干。
senses.why: This is the literal root sense that the moral senses grew away from.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面本义，道德义项正是从它长出去的。

senses.title: Averse to novelty
senses.definition: disinclined toward new ideas, methods, or technology
senses.definitionCN: 对新观念、新方法或新技术不感兴趣甚至抵触
senses.example: The workshop proved averse to digital record-keeping.
senses.exampleCN: 那间作坊始终不愿改用数字记账。
senses.why: Attachment to the familiar is aversion pointed at the new.
senses.whyCN: 恋旧即厌恶指向了新事物。

senses.title: Aversely, in an unfavorable direction
senses.definition: in the adverb aversely, affecting something negatively or disadvantageously
senses.definitionCN: 副词 aversely 中，以负面或不利的方式影响某事
senses.example: The ruling bore aversely on small lenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决对小贷机构不利。
senses.why: Turned against a thing can mean acting against its interest.
senses.whyCN: 「转而背对」也可意味着对其利益不利。

intro.en: Averse comes from Latin aversus, turned away, the past participle of avertere, from ab, away, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: averse 出自拉丁语 aversus「转开的」，是动词 avertere 的过去分词，由 ab（离开）+ vertere（转）构成。

items.en: The turn-root goes back to a reconstructed stem wer- meaning to bend or turn.
items.cn: 「转」的词根可追溯至重构词干 wer-「弯、转」。

items.en: averted, from ab, away, plus vertere, to turn, meant to turn something away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avertere 由 ab「离开」+ vertere「转」构成，意为使转开。

items.en: aversus described a thing or face turned away; morally, turned against.
items.cn: aversus 描述背转的脸或物；道德层面即「反对」。

items.en: English took averse in the late sixteenth century, first literal, soon figurative.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪末借入 averse，先取字面义，很快转为比喻义。

items.en: The pattern averse to fixed in place, and risk aversion later entered economics.
items.cn: averse to 搭配固定下来，「风险规避」后来进入经济学。

items.en: Today averse is almost only predicative: people are averse to things.
items.cn: 如今 averse 几乎只作表语：人对事物 averse。

note.en: Group one gathers the vertere family and its spelling traps; group two gathers words of dislike.
note.cn: 第一组收 vertere 词族及拼写陷阱；第二组收厌恶义场的词。

entries.definition: unfavorable or harmful, acting against; describes conditions, not feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不利的、有害的（起反作用）；形容条件而非心情，勿与 averse 混用。

entries.definition: to turn upside down; shares vertere with averse.
entries.definitionCN: 使倒转；与 averse 同享 vertere 词根。

entries.definition: unwilling and hesitating; milder than averse.
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿、犹豫；语气比 averse 温和。

entries.definition: unwilling out of dislike; also predicative, as loath to admit.
entries.definitionCN: 因厌恶而不愿；同样常作表语，如 loath to admit。

entries.definition: not minded to do something; formal and mild.
entries.definitionCN: 无意于做某事；正式而温和。

entries.definition: naturally opposed in feeling; stronger and more settled than averse.
entries.definitionCN: 天性相斥的；比 averse 更强、更持久。

entries.definition: actively unfriendly; aversion turned into aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 怀敌意的；厌恶转为攻击性的状态。

normalIntro.en: Break it as a-verse: your body turns a verse away, the opposite direction from the thing.
normalIntro.cn: 拆成 a-verse 记：身体像翻页一样把某物翻到背面去。

normal.en: av- from ab- means away: averse turns away, adverse turns against.
normal.cn: av- 出自 ab-「离开」：averse 是转身躲开，adverse 是迎面作对。

normal.en: Risk-averse is the fixed economic collocation.
normal.cn: risk-averse 是经济学固定搭配：规避风险的。

normal.en: not averse to is the polite way of saying quite willing.
normal.cn: not averse to 是「还挺乐意」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: The family holds together: avert, aversion, aversive all carry the same turning.
normal.cn: 词族提示：avert、aversion、aversive 都带同一个「转」。

normal.en: Averse needs a person; adverse needs weather, effects, conditions.
normal.cn: averse 用于人，adverse 用于天气、效果、条件。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders angle away from the offer.
abstract.cn: 感觉肩膀朝提议的反方向偏过去。

abstract.en: Averse is a no spoken with the whole spine.
abstract.cn: averse 是用整条脊柱说出的「不」。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle swinging off north and holding there.
abstract.cn: 想象罗盘针偏开正北并停在那里。

examples.en: Conservative savers are averse to putting money in equities.
examples.cn: 保守的储户不愿把钱投入股市。

examples.en: He was not averse to a little flattery now and then.
examples.cn: 他偶尔也不排斥听两句恭维。

examples.en: The committee remained averse to any delay in the schedule.
examples.cn: 委员会反对日程出现任何延误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恶我死」——那东西一靠近他就喊「恶我死」，赶紧把脸转开

root: 出自拉丁语 aversus「转开的」，为 avertere 的过去分词，由 ab-（离开）+ vertere（转）构成，与 reverse、convert、divert 同属 vertere 词族。16 世纪末进入英语，先表「背向」后转指心理上的「厌恶、反对」，如今几乎只作表语形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from the one root image of turning away: dislike, opposition, unwillingness, risk avoidance, and the technical senses in psychology and older prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「转开」这一根意象展开：厌恶、反对、不情愿、规避风险，以及心理学与旧文体中的技术义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body pivoting so its face no longer meets the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体转过去，脸不再迎向那事物。

branches.en: THE FEELING SIDE: dislike and the opposition it becomes.
branches.cn: 情感一面：反感及其化成的反对。

branches.en: THE WILLINGNESS SIDE: mild turning in not averse to.
branches.cn: 意愿一面：not averse to 中的轻度转开。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL SIDE: risk economics and avoidance learning.
branches.cn: 技术一面：风险经济学与回避学习。

branches.en: THE LITERAL SIDE: turned away in old botany and anatomy.
branches.cn: 字面一面：旧植物学、解剖学中的背向。

branches.en: THE SET SIDE: habit turned from novelty, effect turned against interest.
branches.cn: 定型一面：习惯背对新事物，作用背离利益。

intro.en: Averse is ab- plus versus: the prefix says away, the participle says turned.
intro.cn: averse 的结构是 ab-（离开）加 versus（转开的）。

latinIntro.en: The vertere family is one of Latin's most productive: every turn in English often hides it.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 词族是拉丁语最高产的词族之一：英语里许多「转」都藏着它。

definition_zh: n. 航空；航空业；飞行活动；航空器的制造与使用
definition_en: The design, building and use of aircraft, or the activity of flying them.
core_image: 一整套让人离开地面的行当
scene: 她转行进入航空业，先做地面调度。She moved into aviation, starting with ground dispatch.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aviation 指航空器的设计、制造与使用这一整个领域。

senses.title: The whole field of flight
senses.definition: the design, manufacture and operation of aircraft taken as one field of work
senses.definitionCN: 把航空器的设计、制造与运营视为一个工作领域
senses.example: Aviation employs millions worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 航空业在全球雇用上千万人。
senses.why: Aviation was coined from Latin avis, bird, so it names the human craft of doing what birds do.
senses.whyCN: aviation 由拉丁语 avis「鸟」造出，因此它指人类做鸟所做之事的那门技艺。

senses.title: The activity of flying
senses.definition: the practical activity of flying aircraft, sorted by who flies and for what purpose
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶航空器飞行的实际活动，按谁飞、为何飞来划分
senses.example: General aviation covers private flying.
senses.exampleCN: 通用航空涵盖私人飞行。
senses.why: Once the industry sense was fixed, the same word narrowed to the flying itself, split into civil and military branches.
senses.whyCN: 产业义固定之后，同一个词又收窄到飞行本身，分为民用与军用两支。

intro.en: Aviation is a modern coinage from Latin avis, bird, with the ending -ation; it was formed in French in the 1860s for the idea of mechanical flight.
intro.cn: aviation 是近代由拉丁语 avis「鸟」加 -ation 词尾造出的词；1860 年代在法语中成形，用来指机械飞行这一构想。

items.en: A root meaning bird lies behind aviary and the Latin word avis.
items.cn: 一个表示「鸟」的词根支撑着 aviary 与拉丁语 avis。

items.en: Latin avis meant bird, the natural model for any thought of human flight.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为「鸟」，是人类飞行构想的天然范本。

items.en: Aviarium named a place where birds were kept, giving English aviary.
items.cn: aviarium 指养鸟之处，产生英语 aviary。

items.en: A French writer coined aviation in 1863 from avis plus -ation for aerial navigation.
items.cn: 一位法国作者于 1863 年由 avis 加 -ation 造出 aviation，指空中航行。

items.en: English took the word within three years, while powered flight was still decades away.
items.cn: 英语在三年内就借入该词，而动力飞行还要等上几十年。

items.en: After 1903 the word grew into the name of a whole industry and its regulation.
items.cn: 1903 年之后，这个词扩展为整个产业及其监管的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the avi family; the near-meaning group lists other names for flight as a science or a trade.
note.cn: 形近组保留 avi 词族；近义组列出把飞行当作科学或行业的其他名称。

entries.definition: The act of moving through the air.
Movement of goods or people by air.

entries.definitionCN: 含大气层外空间的飞行领域。

normalIntro.en: Aviation is avis, bird, plus -ation: the human craft of doing what birds do.
normalIntro.cn: aviation 是 avis「鸟」加 -ation：人类做鸟所做之事的那门技艺。

normal.en: Civil aviation is the non-military side.
normal.cn: civil aviation 指非军事的一面。

normal.en: General aviation means private flying.
normal.cn: general aviation 指私人飞行。

normal.en: The word is uncountable.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数。

normal.en: Aviator is the person, aviation is the field.
normal.cn: aviator 是人，aviation 是领域。

normal.en: Aviary shares avis but keeps birds, not planes.
normal.cn: aviary 同出 avis，但装的是鸟不是飞机。

abstract.en: Picture a bird copied in metal and fuel.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用金属与燃油复刻的鸟。

abstract.en: Imagine a hangar, a runway and a tower as one trade.
abstract.cn: 想象机库、跑道与塔台同属一行。

abstract.en: Think of a licence that lets you leave the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张让你离开地面的执照。

examples.en: He studied aviation at a technical college.
examples.cn: 他在一所技术学院学航空。

examples.en: Aviation fuel prices rose again.
examples.cn: 航空燃油价格再次上涨。

examples.en: The authority regulates civil aviation.
examples.cn: 该机构监管民用航空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avi「鸟」（如 aviary 鸟舍）+ -ation「行为、领域」——像鸟一样飞的那门行当，就是 aviation。

root: 拉丁语 avis「鸟」在 1863 年由法语加 -ation 造出 aviation，指空中航行；1903 年动力飞行成功后，词义扩为整个航空产业。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the bird craft: the whole trade of building and running aircraft, and the flying itself sorted by purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是「仿鸟之技」：制造与运营航空器的整个行当，以及按用途划分的飞行本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole trade devoted to leaving the ground
core.cn: 核心意象：一整套让人离开地面的行当

branches.cn: 通用规则下的私人飞行。
两者都在模仿鸟的所为。

intro.en: Aviation is avi plus -ation; the avi root builds aviator, aviary and avionics, while naut gives aeronautics.
intro.cn: aviation 是 avi 加 -ation；avi 词根构成 aviator、aviary 与 avionics，而 naut 则给出 aeronautics。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is avis, bird, and aviarium, a bird house; Greek nautes, sailor, gives the naut of aeronautics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 avis「鸟」与 aviarium「鸟舍」；希腊语 nautes「航行者」给出 aeronautics 中的 naut。

definition_zh: n. 飞行员；飞机驾驶员（语体偏旧或正式）；复数亦指飞行员式太阳镜
definition_en: A person who flies an aircraft, a slightly old-fashioned or formal word for a pilot; in the plural, a style of sunglasses.
core_image: 戴风镜坐在敞开座舱里的那个人
scene: 照片里那位飞行员站在双翼机旁，风镜还挂在额上。In the photograph the aviator stood beside the biplane, goggles still on his forehead.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aviator 指驾驶飞机的人，语体偏旧，常见于早期飞行与军事语境。

senses.title: A person who flies
senses.definition: someone who pilots an aircraft, especially in early or military contexts
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶航空器的人，尤用于早期飞行或军事语境
senses.example: The aviator logged nine hundred hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那位飞行员记录了九百小时飞行。
senses.why: Aviator adds the doer ending -or to the bird root avi, so it names the person who does the bird craft.
senses.whyCN: aviator 在「鸟」词根 avi 上加施事后缀 -or，因此指从事仿鸟之技的那个人。

senses.title: A style named after them
senses.definition: in the plural, a style of sunglasses with large teardrop lenses, from the eyewear of early pilots
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时指一种大水滴形镜片的太阳镜样式，源自早期飞行员的护目镜
senses.example: He wore aviators against the glare.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着飞行员式太阳镜挡强光。
senses.why: The kit of early flyers became a fashion, so the plural of the job title turned into the name of the glasses.
senses.whyCN: 早期飞行员的装备变成了时尚，于是这个职业名称的复数形式成了那种眼镜的名字。

intro.en: Aviator comes from Latin avis, bird, through French aviateur, formed in the 1860s alongside aviation and taken into English soon after.
intro.cn: aviator 出自拉丁语 avis「鸟」，经法语 aviateur 而来；该词于 1860 年代与 aviation 一同造出，随后不久进入英语。

items.en: A root meaning bird also gave the Latin avis and the English word aviary.
items.cn: 一个表示「鸟」的词根同时产生拉丁语 avis 与英语 aviary。

items.en: Latin avis meant bird, the model chosen when flight was still a dream.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为「鸟」，是飞行仍属梦想时选定的范本。

items.en: French formed aviateur from avis on the pattern of navigateur, a navigator.
items.cn: 法语按 navigateur「航行者」的样式，由 avis 造出 aviateur。

items.en: English adopted aviator before anyone had flown a powered machine.
items.cn: 英语在动力飞行出现之前就借入了 aviator。

items.en: Two world wars made aviator the standard formal title in the armed services.
items.cn: 两次世界大战使 aviator 成为军队中的标准正式称谓。

items.en: In the twentieth century the plural named the teardrop sunglasses of military pilots.
items.cn: 二十世纪其复数形式用来指军用飞行员的水滴形太阳镜。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the avi family and one other doer noun; the near-meaning group lists everyday and service words for a flyer.
note.cn: 形近组保留 avi 词族和另一个施事名词；近义组列出表示飞行者的日常与军种用词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a flyer.
A member of an air force.
The people who work in flight.

normalIntro.en: Aviator is avi, bird, plus -or, the doer: the person who does what birds do.
normalIntro.cn: aviator 是 avi「鸟」加 -or「做……的人」：做鸟所做之事的那个人。

normal.en: Pilot is the everyday word; aviator is formal.
normal.cn: pilot 是日常用词，aviator 偏正式。

normal.en: Naval aviator is a set service title.
normal.cn: naval aviator 是固定军种称谓。

normal.en: The female form is aviatrix.
normal.cn: 女性形式是 aviatrix。

normal.en: Aviators also means a shape of sunglasses.
normal.cn: aviators 也指一种太阳镜样式。

normal.en: The field is aviation, the person is aviator.
normal.cn: 领域是 aviation，人是 aviator。

abstract.en: Picture goggles pushed up on a forehead.
abstract.cn: 想象风镜推到额头上。

abstract.en: Imagine an open cockpit and a scarf in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象敞开的座舱与风中的围巾。

abstract.en: Think of a logbook thick with hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满小时数的飞行日志。

examples.en: The young aviator crossed the channel alone.
examples.cn: 那位年轻飞行员独自飞越海峡。

examples.en: Naval aviators train on carriers.
examples.cn: 海军飞行员在航母上训练。

examples.en: She bought a pair of aviators.
examples.cn: 她买了一副飞行员式太阳镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avi「鸟」+ -ator「做……的人」——像鸟一样飞的人，就是 aviator 飞行员。

root: 拉丁语 avis「鸟」在法语中按 navigateur 的样式造出 aviateur，英语 1866 年借作 aviator；两次世界大战后成为军中正式称谓，复数又指飞行员式太阳镜。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from the same kit: the person who flies like a bird, and the eyewear that person made famous.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项出自同一套装备：像鸟一样飞行的人，以及被这个人带火的那副眼镜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in goggles sitting in an open cockpit
core.cn: 核心意象：戴风镜坐在敞开座舱里的那个人

branches.cn: 站在双翼机旁的飞行员。

branches.en: A logbook of nine hundred hours.
The kit named after its wearer.

intro.en: Aviator is avi plus -ator; the same doer ending builds navigator and operator, while -trix marks the female form.
intro.cn: aviator 是 avi 加 -ator；同一施事后缀构成 navigator 与 operator，而 -trix 标记女性形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is avis, bird; the ending -ator is the Latin agent suffix, and Greek nautes gives navigator beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 avis「鸟」；词尾 -ator 是拉丁语施事后缀，旁边的希腊语 nautes 给出 navigator。

definition_zh: 避免；躲开；回避
definition_en: to stay away from something or prevent it from happening
core_image: 脚在最后一刻抬起来，跨过地上的水洼
scene: 路面刚下过雨，行人绕开积水。She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.
sceneCN: 这里 avoid 是「躲开」（第 1 个义项：避开某个具体的东西）；句意是她侧身让开，避开了那摊水。

derivatives.zh: 由 avoid 加 -ance 构成，义为「回避；避免」
由 avoid 加 -able 构成，义为「可避免的」
由 avoidable 加 un- 构成，义为「不可避免的」

senses.title: Stay away from
senses.definition: to keep away from a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 远离某人、某地或某物
senses.example: She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.
senses.exampleCN: 她侧身让开，避开了那摊水。
senses.why: Avoid comes from Old French esvuidier, to empty out, from vuide, empty; to avoid a place was to leave it empty and then to keep clear of it.
senses.whyCN: avoid 来自古法语 esvuidier「清空」，源于 vuide「空的」；把某地腾空，就是离开它，再引申为躲开它。

senses.title: Prevent from happening
senses.definition: to stop something bad from happening
senses.definitionCN: 阻止不好的事情发生
senses.example: Careful driving can avoid many accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 谨慎驾驶可以避免许多事故。
senses.why: If you keep clear of a risk, the bad event never occurs, so the same verb came to mean preventing it.
senses.whyCN: 躲开风险，坏事就不会发生，于是同一个动词又表示「防止」。

senses.title: Not do something
senses.definition: to choose not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 有意不去做某事
senses.example: He avoided answering the question.
senses.exampleCN: 他回避了那个问题。
senses.why: Leaving a thing empty extends to leaving an action undone, which is why avoid often takes an -ing form.
senses.whyCN: 把某物腾空可以延伸到把某个动作搁下不做，因此 avoid 后面常接动名词。

intro.en: Avoid began as a word about emptying a place.
intro.cn: avoid 最初说的是把某处腾空。

items.en: vacuus meant 'empty'.
items.cn: vacuus 意为「空的」。

items.en: vuide meant 'empty'.
items.cn: vuide 意为「空的」。

items.en: esvuidier meant 'to empty out'.
items.cn: esvuidier 意为「清空」。

items.en: avoiden meant 'to leave or withdraw'.
items.cn: avoiden 意为「离开、退出」。

items.en: The sense shifted to keeping clear of things.
items.cn: 词义转向「躲开、避开」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the v sound; the near-meaning group gives ways of getting out of harm.
note.cn: 形近组都含 v 音；近义组是表示脱离危险的词。

normalIntro.en: Avoid is about leaving a space empty, and so keeping clear of trouble.
normalIntro.cn: avoid 讲的是把空间让空，从而避开麻烦。

normal.en: Avoid is followed by an -ing form, not an infinitive.
normal.cn: avoid 后接动名词，不接不定式。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: a-VOID.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Avoidance is the noun and avoidable the adjective.
normal.cn: 名词是 avoidance，形容词是 avoidable。

normal.en: You avoid a thing, not avoid from a thing.
normal.cn: avoid 直接带宾语，不加 from。

normal.en: Unavoidable means it cannot be prevented.
normal.cn: unavoidable 意为无法避免的。

abstract.en: See a foot lifting just before a puddle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在水洼前抬起。

abstract.en: See a person turning a corner to miss a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人拐过街角避开人群。

abstract.en: See a hand pulling back from a hot pan.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从热锅前缩回。

examples.en: She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.
examples.cn: 她侧身让开，避开了那摊水。

examples.en: Careful driving can avoid many accidents.
examples.cn: 谨慎驾驶可以避免许多事故。

examples.en: He avoided answering the question.
examples.cn: 他回避了那个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 void（空的）：把前面的空间让空，人就走开了，麻烦也就避开了。

root: 源自古法语 esvuidier「清空」，由 es- 与 vuide「空的」构成，上溯拉丁语 vacuus「空」；由腾空、离开引申为躲开、避免。

sensesIntro.en: Leaving a place, a risk or an action all begin with making space.
sensesIntro.cn: 离开地方、躲开风险、搁下动作，都从「让出空间」开始。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot lifting to leave an empty space.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚抬起，让出一块空地。

intro.en: The void root, 'empty', also gives void, devoid and vacancy.
intro.cn: 词根 void 意为「空」，也构成 void、devoid 与 vacancy。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus, 'empty', supplies the base for this family of emptying words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus「空」为这一族「清空」词提供词基。

a time left empty of work

definition_zh: n. 避免；回避；躲开；（法律上）宣告无效；撤销
definition_en: The act of keeping away from or preventing something; in law, the making of a document void.
core_image: 提前绕开那个坑的那一步
scene: 他把回避冲突当成习惯，结果问题越积越多。He made avoidance of conflict a habit, and the problems piled up.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：avoidance 指有意躲开或防止某事发生这一行为。

senses.title: Keeping away from
senses.definition: the practice of staying clear of a person, subject or situation
senses.definitionCN: 有意远离某人、某话题或某处境的做法
senses.example: His avoidance of eye contact was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 他明显在回避目光接触。
senses.why: Avoid came from a French phrase meaning to make empty, so avoidance is the act of clearing something out of your path.
senses.whyCN: avoid 源自意为「清空」的法语短语，因此 avoidance 就是把某物从自己路径上清开的行为。

senses.title: Preventing an outcome
senses.definition: the deliberate prevention of an unwanted event, as in arranging affairs so a burden never falls due
senses.definitionCN: 有意防止不良事件发生，例如事先安排事务使某项负担不落到头上
senses.example: Tax avoidance is legal, unlike evasion.
senses.exampleCN: 避税合法，与逃税不同。
senses.why: The same clearing idea applies before the event, so the word covers arranging affairs in advance.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「清空」思路用在事件之前，于是这个词也涵盖事先安排事务。

senses.title: Making void in law
senses.definition: in legal use, the act of making a contract or instrument void
senses.definitionCN: 在法律用法中，指使合同或文书无效的行为
senses.example: The clause provided for avoidance of the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款规定了保单的撤销。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original empty meaning literally: the document is emptied of legal force.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项字面保留了「空」的本义：文书的法律效力被清空。

intro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance; avoid comes from Anglo-French avoider, to clear out, from es-, out, and vuide, empty, related to Latin vacuus.
intro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance；avoid 来自盎格鲁法语 avoider「清空」，由 es-「向外」与 vuide「空」构成，与拉丁语 vacuus 相关。

items.en: Latin vacuus meant empty, the source of vacant and vacuum.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus 意为「空的」，是 vacant 与 vacuum 的来源。

items.en: Old French vuide meant empty, and vuidier meant to empty out.
items.cn: 古法语 vuide 意为「空」，vuidier 意为「腾空」。

items.en: With es-, out, prefixed, avoider meant to clear out or withdraw.
items.cn: 加上 es-「向外」构成 avoider，意为「清空、撤出」。

items.en: Middle English avoiden meant to remove, expel or leave empty.
items.cn: 中古英语 avoiden 意为「移走、驱逐、腾空」。

items.en: The noun is recorded early, kept in law for making a document void.
items.cn: 该名词出现很早，在法律中保留「使文书无效」之义。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the verb had settled into keeping clear of something.
items.cn: 到十五世纪动词已定型为「躲开某事物」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the void family; the near-meaning group lists other words for staying clear of something.
note.cn: 形近组保留 void 词族；近义组列出其他表示远离某事物的词。

entries.definition: Empty, or of no legal force.

normalIntro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance: the act of emptying your path of something you do not want.
normalIntro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance：把不想要的东西从自己路径上清开的行为。

normal.en: Tax avoidance is legal; tax evasion is not.
normal.cn: tax avoidance 合法，tax evasion 不合法。

normal.en: The pattern is avoidance of plus a noun.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 avoidance of 加名词。

normal.en: Avoidance behaviour is a psychology term.
normal.cn: avoidance behaviour 是心理学术语。

normal.en: The adjective pair is avoidable and unavoidable.
normal.cn: 形容词一对是 avoidable 与 unavoidable。

normal.en: A set clause opens with a phrase about doubt.
normal.cn: 有个固定条款以「为免生疑义」开头。

abstract.en: Picture a step sideways around a hole.
abstract.cn: 想象绕开坑洞的侧向一步。

abstract.en: Imagine a gaze that never lands on yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一道从不落到你身上的目光。

abstract.en: Think of a contract drained of its force.
abstract.cn: 想象一份被抽走效力的合同。

examples.en: Avoidance of delay saved the contract.
examples.cn: 避免延误保住了这份合同。

examples.en: Fear often shows itself as avoidance.
examples.cn: 恐惧常表现为回避。

examples.en: The policy allows avoidance for fraud.
examples.cn: 该保单允许因欺诈而撤销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avoid「躲开、清空」+ -ance「行为」——把不想要的东西从路上清开，这一行为就是 avoidance。

root: 拉丁语 vacuus「空」经古法语 vuide 加 es-「向外」成 avoider「清空」，入中古英语作 avoiden「躲开」；加 -ance 成 avoidance，法律中保留「使无效」的本义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses empty something out of the way: a person or topic, an unwanted outcome, or the legal force of a document.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在把某物清开：某人或某话题、不想要的结果，或文书的法律效力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the step taken early to go around the hole
core.cn: 核心意象：提前绕开那个坑的那一步

branches.en: A gaze kept off the other person.
branches.cn: 不落在对方身上的目光。

branches.en: Conflict pushed out of the way.
Affairs arranged so no tax falls due.
branches.cn: 安排得不产生税负的事务。

branches.en: A policy emptied of legal force.
branches.cn: 被抽走法律效力的保单。

branches.en: Both clear the path before trouble.
branches.cn: 两者都在麻烦之前清出路径。

intro.en: Avoidance is avoid plus -ance; avoid hides es-, out, and vuide, empty, which also give void and vacuum.
intro.cn: avoidance 是 avoid 加 -ance；avoid 里藏着 es-「向外」与 vuide「空」，它们也产生 void 与 vacuum。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is vacuus, empty, and vacare, to be empty; the -ance ending is Latin -antia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 vacuus「空」与 vacare「空着」；-ance 词尾即拉丁语 -antia。

definition_zh: 公开承认；坦率声明；宣称
definition_en: to state openly and firmly that something is true or that one holds a view
core_image: 站到众人面前，把心里的话大声说出口
scene: 烛光下，他向全家说出决定。She avowed her loyalty to the old republic.
sceneCN: 这里 avow 指「公开声明」（第 1 个义项：坦然宣告立场）；句意：她公开表达了对旧共和国的忠诚。

senses.title: To declare openly
senses.definition: to state a belief, loyalty, or intention openly and firmly
senses.definitionCN: 公开而坚定地陈述信念、忠诚或意图
senses.example: He avowed his intention to run for mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 他公开宣布参选市长的打算。
senses.why: The Latin root vocare, to call, gives the word its speaking-out loudness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 vocare「呼唤」赋予这个词大声说出的性质。

senses.title: To admit or acknowledge
senses.definition: to accept responsibility or authorship of something done
senses.definitionCN: 承认对已做之事负有责任或为其作者
senses.example: No group avowed the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何组织宣称对袭击负责。
senses.why: Owning a deed publicly is calling it one's own.
senses.whyCN: 公开认领一个行为，就是把它唤作自己的。

senses.title: To affirm under oath or vow
senses.definition: in legal and older use, to affirm solemnly, as a vow or deposition
senses.definitionCN: 法律及旧式用法中庄重确认，如立誓、作证
senses.example: The witness avowed the statement before the court.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在法庭上郑重确认了陈述。
senses.why: Avow grew beside the noun vow: speech fortified by oath.
senses.whyCN: avow 与名词 vow 并肩生长：以誓言加固的言语。

senses.title: Avowed, as a belief or enemy
senses.definition: in participial adjective use, openly declared or professed
senses.definitionCN: 分词形容词用法，指公开宣称的
senses.example: She was an avowed vegetarian by fourteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十四岁就公开吃素了。
senses.why: The participle pins the open declaration onto the person.
senses.whyCN: 分词把公开声明钉在了人身上。

senses.title: To justify or defend a course
senses.definition: to stand behind a policy or act, endorsing it before others
senses.definitionCN: 为他人的政策或行为公开背书
senses.example: The party avowed the minister's hard line.
senses.exampleCN: 该党为部长的强硬路线背书。
senses.why: Speaking for another act keeps the loud-voice root.
senses.whyCN: 为他人的行为发声，仍是那个「大声呼唤」的词根。

senses.title: To profess art, faith, or craft
senses.definition: to present oneself openly as a member of a profession or faith
senses.definitionCN: 公开以某职业或信仰者身份自处
senses.example: He avows himself a student of the old masters.
senses.exampleCN: 他自认是古典大师的学徒。
senses.why: Naming yourself aloud completes the act of calling.
senses.whyCN: 大声说出自己的名字，完成了「呼唤」这个动作。

senses.title: Avowal, the noun of the act
senses.definition: in the noun avowal, the declaration itself
senses.definitionCN: 名词 avowal 中，指声明这一行为或文本
senses.example: Her avowal surprised the quiet committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的公开表态让安静的委员会吃了一惊。
senses.why: The speech-act freezes into a document or moment.
senses.whyCN: 言语行为凝固成文件或时刻。

senses.title: Avowedly, in open manner
senses.definition: in the adverb avowedly, admittedly and openly
senses.definitionCN: 副词 avowedly 中，指公开地、无可否认地
senses.example: The book is avowedly polemical.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书公然是一部论战之作。
senses.why: The adverb carries the openness into the manner of the act.
senses.whyCN: 副词把「公开」带进了行为的方式。

intro.en: Avow comes from Old French avouer, from Latin advocare, to call to one's aid, from ad, to, plus vocare, to call; the sense passed from advocating to owning and declaring.
intro.cn: avow 经古法语 avouer 出自拉丁语 advocare「召来相助」，由 ad（向）+ vocare（呼唤）构成；词义从「拥护」演变为「认领、声明」。

items.en: The call-root is the reconstructed wek-, to speak or call.
items.cn: 「呼唤」词根出自重构词干 wek-「说、喊」。

items.en: advocare meant to summon to one's side, hence to support.
items.cn: advocare 意为召至身边，引申为拥护。

items.en: avouer meant to acknowledge or claim as one's own, as a lord his act or a patron his cause.
items.cn: 古法语 avouer 意为认领：领主认领行为，庇护人认领事业。

items.en: Middle English avowed first carried the sense of defending or upholding a cause.
items.cn: 中古英语的 avowed 先表拥护、捍卫某事业。

items.en: The modern sense of open declaration consolidated, alongside the participle avowed.
items.cn: 16 世纪「公开声明」义定型，分词 avowed 同步确立。

items.en: Today avow lives mostly in avowed, avowal, and avowedly.
items.cn: 如今 avow 多以 avowed、avowal、avowedly 的形态活跃。

note.en: Group one gathers the vocare family and a vow trap; group two gathers words of declaring.
note.cn: 第一组收 vocare 词族及 vow 陷阱；第二组收声明义场的词。

entries.definition: a solemn promise, from Latin votum; shorter but historically distinct from avow.
entries.definitionCN: 庄严誓约，出自拉丁语 votum；与 avow 形近，词源各有脉络。

entries.definition: to speak for a cause; the Latin ancestor's direct heir.
entries.definitionCN: 拥护、倡导；拉丁祖先的直接后裔。

entries.definition: to declare one's faith or skill openly.
to admit the truth or existence of something.
to deny any connection with or responsibility for.
entries.definitionCN: 否认关联或责任；avow 的反义词。

entries.definition: to bear formal witness to something.

normalIntro.en: Hear a-vow inside the word: a vow spoken out loud, in front of everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 词中听见 a-vow：当众说出的誓言。

normal.en: avow and vow differ in spelling history but rhyme in function: both are speech with weight.
normal.cn: avow 与 vow 拼写史不同而功能押韵：都是有分量的言语。

normal.en: The opposite is disavow: add dis- to deny.
normal.cn: 反义词是 disavow：加 dis- 即否认。

normal.en: an avowed enemy is the classic collocation.
normal.cn: an avowed enemy 是经典搭配：公开的敌人。

normal.en: avowal is the noun; keep the -al ending like refusal.
normal.cn: 名词是 avowal，词尾 -al 同 refusal。

normal.en: avowedly means admittedly, as in avowedly biased.
normal.cn: avowedly 意为自认地，如 avowedly biased。

abstract.en: Feel the throat open before the crowd does.
abstract.cn: 感觉喉咙在人群之前先张开了。

abstract.en: Avow is a flag run up the pole in daylight.
abstract.cn: avow 是大白日里升起的旗帜。

abstract.en: Picture ink drying on a signed confession.
abstract.cn: 想象签了字的自白书上墨迹渐干。

examples.en: The committee avowed its support for the reforms.
examples.cn: 委员会公开表态支持改革。

examples.en: An avowed pacifist, he refused the officer's commission.
examples.cn: 作为公开的和平主义者，他拒绝了军官委任。

examples.en: His avowal of guilt ended the long trial.
examples.cn: 他认罪的自白终结了漫长的审判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我傲」——他站上椅子「我傲！」，当众承认全是我干的

root: 经古法语 avouer 出自拉丁语 advocare「召来相助」（ad 向 + vocare 呼唤），词义从「拥护」演为「认领、公开声明」；13 世纪进入中古英语，16 世纪「公开声明」义定型。与 vow（出自 votum）拼写相近但词源脉络不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one gesture, speech made public: declaring belief, owning deeds, sworn affirmations, and the derived forms avowed, avowal, avowedly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一个手势——把话说到明处：宣示信念、认领行为、立誓确认，以及派生形式 avowed、avowal、avowedly。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice lifted in public, claiming a thing as one's own.
core.cn: 核心意象：当众扬声，把某事认作己出。

branches.en: THE SELF SIDE: declaring one's beliefs and one's identity.
branches.cn: 自我一面：宣示信念与身份。

branches.en: THE OWNERSHIP SIDE: claiming one's deeds, for good or ill.
branches.cn: 认领一面：认下自己的行为，无论好坏。

branches.en: THE SOLEMN SIDE: speech fortified by vow and court.
branches.cn: 庄严一面：以誓言与法庭加固的言语。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR SIDE: the participle and adverb of openness.
branches.cn: 语法一面：表示公开的分词与副词。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ACT SIDE: endorsements and the frozen declaration.
branches.cn: 公开行为一面：背书与定格的声明。

intro.en: Avow descends from advocare, ad plus vocare; the d dropped out in Old French.
intro.cn: avow 承自 advocare（ad + vocare），那个 d 在古法语中脱落了。

latinIntro.en: Vocare generated the great calling family of English: voice, vocal, vocation, invoke, advocate.
latinIntro.cn: vocare 衍生出英语庞大的「呼唤」家族：voice、vocal、vocation、invoke、advocate。

definition_zh: 奖；奖品；授予；判给
definition_en: a prize given for achievement, or to give such a prize officially
core_image: 一只奖杯被递到伸出的双手上
scene: 典礼上掌声响起。The judge awarded her the first prize.
sceneCN: 这里 award 是「授予」（第 2 个义项：正式把奖项或款项给某人）；句意是评委把一等奖授予了她。

derivatives.zh: 由 award 加 -ee 构成，义为「获奖者」
由 award 与 winning 复合而成，义为「获奖的；屡获殊荣的」

senses.title: A prize
senses.definition: something given to someone for an achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而发给某人的东西
senses.example: She received an award for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她因研究成果获得了一个奖项。
senses.why: Award comes from Old French eswarder, to judge, so a prize is what a judge decides to give.
senses.whyCN: award 来自古法语 eswarder「评判」，所以奖项就是评判者决定给出的东西。

senses.title: Give officially
senses.definition: to give money or a prize officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式发给钱款或奖项
senses.example: The judge awarded her the first prize.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把一等奖授予了她。
senses.why: The noun for a decided gift turned into the verb for the deciding and giving.
senses.whyCN: 表示判定给予之物的名词，转成了表示判定并给予的动词。

senses.title: Decide legally
senses.definition: to decide that someone should receive money in a court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁定某人应得钱款
senses.example: The court awarded damages to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判给这家人损害赔偿金。
senses.why: A judge's decision is the oldest sense, and the courtroom is where the giving is most formal.
senses.whyCN: 评判者的裁定是最古老的义项，而法庭正是这种给予最正式的场合。

intro.en: Award is a word about judging before it is a word about prizes.
intro.cn: award 先是关于评判的词，然后才关于奖品。

items.en: warder meant 'to guard or watch'.
items.cn: warder 意为「看守、注视」。

items.en: eswarder meant 'to judge'.
items.cn: eswarder 意为「评判」。

items.en: awarder meant 'to decide'.
items.cn: awarder 意为「裁定」。

items.en: award meant a decision of a judge.
items.cn: award 意为法官的裁定。

items.en: The prize sense became the most common.
items.cn: 奖项义成为最常用的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw opening; the near-meaning group gives prizes and grants.
note.cn: 形近组都以 aw 开头；近义组是表示奖品与授予的词。

normalIntro.en: An award is what a judge gives, while a reward is what you earn for service.
normalIntro.cn: award 是评判者给出的，reward 是因服务而得到的回报。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable: a-WARD.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Use award for prizes and official payments.
normal.cn: award 用于奖项与正式款项。

normal.en: A reward is usually money for help or effort.
normal.cn: reward 通常是因帮助或努力得到的钱。

normal.en: The noun and the verb have the same form.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形。

normal.en: An award-winning film is one that has won prizes.
normal.cn: award-winning 指获奖的。

abstract.en: See a trophy passed into two open hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一只奖杯被递到张开的双手上。

abstract.en: See a judge striking a small hammer.
abstract.cn: 想象法官敲下小锤。

abstract.en: See a name read out and a row of heads turning.
abstract.cn: 想象有人念出一个名字，一排脑袋转过去。

examples.en: She received an award for her research.
examples.cn: 她因研究成果获得了一个奖项。

examples.en: The judge awarded her the first prize.
examples.cn: 评委把一等奖授予了她。

examples.en: The court awarded damages to the family.
examples.cn: 法庭判给这家人损害赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ward（看）：评判者看准了谁做得好，就把奖递过去，这就是授予。

root: 源自古法语 eswarder「评判」，与 warder「看守、注视」同源，经盎格鲁-诺曼语 awarder「裁定」进入英语；由法官裁定引申为授予奖项。

sensesIntro.en: A prize, an official gift and a legal ruling are all one judged decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 奖品、正式给予与法律裁定，都是同一个「经评判而给出」的决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup handed into waiting hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只奖杯被递到等待的双手上。

intro.en: The ward root, 'to watch', also gives ward, guard and reward.
intro.cn: 词根 ward 意为「看守」，也构成 ward、guard 与 reward。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family comes from Germanic watch words through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这一族词经法语来自日耳曼语表示「看守」的词。

items.meaning: a guard or a protected area
one who looks after a household

definition_zh: 意识到的；知道的；察觉到的
definition_en: knowing that something exists or is happening
core_image: 一个人忽然停下，侧耳听见远处的警笛
scene: 街角的行人同时抬起头。Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
sceneCN: 这里 aware 是「意识到的」（第 1 个义项：知道某事存在或正在发生）；句意是每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。

pos.zh: 形容词：意识到的；知道的；察觉到的

derivatives.zh: 由 aware 加 -ness 构成，义为「意识；认识」
由 aware 加 un- 构成，义为「未察觉的」
由 self 与 aware 复合而成，义为「有自我意识的」

senses.title: Knowing something exists
senses.definition: knowing that something exists or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事存在或正在发生
senses.example: Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。
senses.why: Aware is an old adjective from ware, watchful; to be aware is to have your attention on something.
senses.whyCN: aware 是古形容词 ware「警觉的」的变体；aware 就是注意力落在某物上。

senses.title: Informed about a fact
senses.definition: having knowledge of a fact or situation
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某个事实或情况
senses.example: Are you aware that the office closes early today?
senses.exampleCN: 你知道办公室今天提前关门吗？
senses.why: Watchfulness grows into knowledge, so aware also means having information, especially information others may not have.
senses.whyCN: 警觉会发展成知识，所以 aware 也指掌握信息，尤其是别人未必知道的信息。

intro.en: Aware began as a word for being watchful.
intro.cn: aware 最初表示「警觉的」。

items.en: wær meant 'cautious or watchful'.
items.cn: wær 意为「谨慎、警觉」。

items.en: gewær meant 'aware'.
items.cn: gewær 意为「觉察到的」。

items.en: aware kept the sense of being watchful.
items.cn: aware 保留了警觉之义。

items.en: aware shifted toward knowing.
items.cn: aware 转向「知道」。

items.en: Aware of is now the usual pattern.
items.cn: 如今常用 aware of 的结构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the a- opening; the near-meaning group gives kinds of knowing.
note.cn: 形近组都以 a- 开头；近义组是表示知道与留心的词。

normalIntro.en: Aware is watchfulness turned into knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: aware 是警觉变成了知识。

normal.en: Aware of is the usual pattern, and aware that also works.
normal.cn: 常用 aware of，也可接 aware that。

normal.en: The noun is awareness, not aware.
normal.cn: 名词是 awareness。

normal.en: Unaware means not knowing.
normal.cn: unaware 意为不知道的。

normal.en: Aware is not used before a noun in most speech.
normal.cn: 多数口语中 aware 不放在名词前。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-WARE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a walker stopping and turning an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象行人停下脚步侧耳倾听。

abstract.en: See a light switching on in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗房里一盏灯亮起。

abstract.en: See a hand raised to warn the person ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起提醒前面的人。

examples.en: Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
examples.cn: 每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。

examples.en: Are you aware that the office closes early today?
examples.cn: 你知道办公室今天提前关门吗？

examples.en: She became aware of soft footsteps behind her.
examples.cn: 她察觉到身后有轻轻的脚步声。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ware（警觉）：眼睛和耳朵先醒过来，心里也就知道了。

root: 源自古英语 wær「谨慎、警觉」及其复合形式 gewær「觉察到的」，属日耳曼语系；由「警觉」引申为「知道、意识到」。

sensesIntro.en: Watchfulness and knowledge are two ends of the same attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 警觉与知识，是同一种注意力的两端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ear turning toward a distant sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：耳朵转向远处的声音。

branches.en: aware that the shop is closed

intro.en: The ware root, 'watchful', also gives beware, wary and awareness.
intro.cn: 词根 ware 意为「警觉」，也构成 beware、wary 与 awareness。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这一族词来自日耳曼语。

items.meaning: to see or become aware of

definition_zh: 意识；认识；察觉
definition_en: the state of knowing that something exists or is important
core_image: 一束灯光照亮原本黑暗的角落
scene: 社区公告栏前围了一圈人。The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
sceneCN: 这里 awareness 是「意识」（第 1 个义项：知道某事存在或重要）；句意是这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「意识到的」，awareness 由其加 -ness 构成
由 aware 加 un- 构成，义为「未察觉的」
由 unaware 加 -ness 构成，义为「未察觉」

senses.title: The state of knowing
senses.definition: the state of knowing that something exists
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事存在的状态
senses.example: The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。
senses.why: Awareness is aware plus -ness, and the suffix turns a passing state of attention into a lasting condition of mind.
senses.whyCN: awareness 是 aware 加 -ness，后缀把一时的注意变成一种持续的心智状态。

senses.title: Public understanding
senses.definition: the extent to which people know and care about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某个议题了解与关心的程度
senses.example: Public awareness of the disease has grown.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对这种疾病的认识提高了。
senses.why: When many people hold the same knowledge, awareness becomes a social measure rather than a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共享同一种认识时，awareness 就从私人感受变成了社会性的衡量指标。

intro.en: Awareness is the noun built on the old word for watchfulness.
intro.cn: awareness 是建在古「警觉」一词上的名词。

items.en: wær meant 'watchful'.
items.cn: wær 意为「警觉的」。

items.en: aware meant 'watchful, then knowing'.
items.cn: aware 意为「警觉的，后为知道的」。

items.en: The suffix -ness made a state noun.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 构成表示状态的名词。

items.en: awareness meant the state of being aware.
items.cn: awareness 意为「觉察的状态」。

items.en: It also names public attention to issues.
items.cn: 如今也指公众对议题的关注。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aware base; the near-meaning group gives kinds of mental attention.
note.cn: 形近组都含 aware 词基；近义组是表示心理注意的词。

entries.definition: the state of being awake and aware

normalIntro.en: Awareness is watchfulness made permanent and shared.
normalIntro.cn: awareness 是警觉被固定下来，并被许多人共享。

normal.en: Awareness is uncountable, so it takes no plural.
normal.cn: awareness 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: The verb pattern is raise awareness, not make awareness.
normal.cn: 搭配是 raise awareness。

normal.en: Awareness of something names the thing noticed.
normal.cn: awareness of 后接被察觉的对象。

normal.en: The base adjective is aware, not awareness.
normal.cn: 基础形容词是 aware。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-WARE-ness.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a lamp lighting one dark corner of a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮房间里黑暗的一角。

abstract.en: See a crowd all reading the same poster.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人都在读同一张海报。

abstract.en: See a ribbon pinned on many coats.
abstract.cn: 想象许多外套上都别着同一条丝带。

examples.en: The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
examples.cn: 这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。

examples.en: Public awareness of the disease has grown.
examples.cn: 公众对这种疾病的认识提高了。

examples.en: She spoke with great awareness of the risks.
examples.cn: 她讲话时对这些风险有很清楚的认识。

dict_mnemonic.text: aware（警觉的）加 -ness（状态）：警觉停在心里成了常态，就是意识。

root: 由 aware 加名词后缀 -ness 构成；aware 源自古英语 wær「警觉」，属日耳曼语系；由「警觉的状态」引申为「意识、认识」。

sensesIntro.en: A private state of knowing and a public level of attention are the same noun at two scales.
sensesIntro.cn: 私人的知道与公共的关注度，是同一个名词的两种尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light reaching a dark corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光照到黑暗的角落。

intro.en: The -ness suffix turns adjectives into state nouns, as in awareness and kindness.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态名词，如 awareness 与 kindness。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, while the suffix is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自日耳曼语，后缀是英语本族成分。
